articleTitle: Advances in Raman amplifier fibers
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: Summary form only given, as follows. Raman fiber lasers and amplifiers will play an increasing role in future optical fiber communication systems. Recent progress in the development of special Raman fibers is described. We particularly focus on high /spl Delta/n germanosilicate and phosphosilicate fibers.

articleTitle: Holey new fibers
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: Summary form only given. Photonic crystal fibre (PCF) consists of a thread of glass with an array of microscopic air holes running along its length. The first working example-"endlessly single-mode" fibre-was reported at OFC in 1996. Since then, there has been a series of break-throughs that is leading to a radical enhancement in the possibilities of optical fibres. The disruptive implications of the new technology are just beginning to be worked out. The tutorial will cover the history, physics and applications of PCF.

articleTitle: Optical label switching
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: Summary form only given. The design and implementation of a optical label switched router for packet switched WDM networks will be presented. The algorithms of generating optical labels, look-up tables, routing protocols, and a scaleable network architecture similar to IP/MPLS in optical domain will also be discussed.

articleTitle: New standards for optical internetworking
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: Presents a brief biography of the author.

articleTitle: Reducing PMD impairments
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: Summary form only given. We review the optical and electrical PMD compensation schemes that can be found in the literature. Because of the statistical nature of PMD, most of them are composed of an adaptive counteractive element, a feedback signal and a tracking algorithm. We also mention the importance of PMD statistics emulation and of the long-term field experiments related to PMD.

articleTitle: OFC'01 invited talk the internet of the future
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: Summary form only given. A remarkable expansion in the use of the Internet has spurred innovations in the networking infrastructure as well as exploration of new networked applications. But what we observe today is just a tip of the iceberg. This talk describes an array of potential new applications that will be running on the Internet of the future, and highlights the Internet infrastructure research - including the next generation optical networking and ultra high-speed wireless research - that are being pursued to bring about the new reality.

articleTitle: Impact of intermediate traffic grouping on the dimensioning of multi-granularity optical networks
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We demonstrate the interest of multi-granularity optical networks to decrease the number of ports for the optical switching matrices by grouping some wavelengths into bands and some bands into fibers at some intermediate nodes.

articleTitle: A single-chip linear optical amplifier
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: The performance of a new, single-chip linear optical amplifier (LOA) is compared to a semiconductor optical amplifier and an EDFA. Bit-error-rate measurements of the LOA show no power penalty in a 10 Gb/s WDM transmission system test.

articleTitle: 1296-port MEMS transparent optical crossconnect with 2.07 petabit/s switch capacity
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: A 1296-port MEMS transparent optical crossconnect with 5.1dB/spl plusmn/1.1dB insertion loss at 1550 nm is reported. Measured worst-case optical crosstalk in a fabric was n38 dB and nominal switching rise/fall times were 5 ms. A 2.07 petabit/s switch capacity was verified upon cross-connecting a forty-channel by 40 Gb/s DWDM data stream through a prototype fabric.

articleTitle: 10.92-Tb/s (273/spl times/40-Gb/s) triple-band/ultra-dense WDM optical-repeatered transmission experiment
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: With LD-pumped gain-shifted thulium-doped fiber amplifiers, polarization interleave multiplexing combined with wavelength/polarization demultiplexing for 50-GHz-spaced 40-Gb/s/ch WDM signals, and a transmission line optimization for triple-band systems, the first 10-Tb/s WDM transmission in single fiber using S-, C- and L-bands is demonstrated.

articleTitle: Design of near optimum electrical equalizers for optical transmission in the presence of PMD
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: An adaptive Viterbi equalizer and a decision feedback equaliser (DFE) for nonlinear intersymbol interference using a state-based probabilistic approach is proposed. The Viterbi equalizer design is suitable for high data rates and outperforms other concepts for high PMD.

articleTitle: Chromatic dispersion monitoring and automated compensation for NRZ and RZ data using clock regeneration and fading without adding signaling
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We show that the clock signal can be extracted from both NRZ and RZ data, and that this extracted signal power represents the total accumulated dispersion. We also demonstrate dynamic dispersion compensation at 10 Gbit/s using the extracted power as a control signal.

articleTitle: Fast eye monitor for 10 Gbit/s and its application for optical PMD compensation
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: The excellent correlation between high speed eye monitor signal and BER shows the potential for fast tracking of eye fluctuations and performance monitoring. PMD compensation experiments at 10 Gbit/s demonstrate the performance of a fast eye monitor used as feedback signal.

articleTitle: Auto-discovery of shared risk link groups
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We propose location-based techniques for the automatic discovery of shared risk link groups (SRLGs) in transport networks, which are fundamental inputs for failure risk management. The benefit of these techniques is to enhance or replace the flawed, manually maintained databases used today to support SRLG management.

articleTitle: Automatic PMD compensation at 40 Gbit/s and 80 Gbit/s using a 3-dimensional DOP evaluation for feedback
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We demonstrate that polarization scrambling combined with degree of polarization (DOP) evaluation enables polarization mode dispersion (PMD) compensation without feedback fading due to varying input polarization. PMD of an installed fiber as well as PMD of an emulator was successfully compensated.

articleTitle: Performance demonstration of a fast-tunable transmitter and burst-mode packet receiver for HORNET
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We demonstrate error-free packet-over-WDM transmission using a fast-tunable transmitter and novel packet receiver. The transmitter tunes fine (0.8 nm) and. wide (/spl sim/30 nm) within 15 ns, while the receiver receives unframed packets by bit-synchronizing in 40 ns.

articleTitle: 10.2 Tbit/s (256x42.7 Gbit/s PDM/WDM) transmission over 100 km TeraLight/sup TM/ fiber with 1.28 bit/s/Hz spectral efficiency
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We demonstrate the transmission of 256 polarization-division and wavelength-division multiplexed channels at 42.7 Gbit/s rate over 100 km of TeraLight/sup TM/ fiber. An overall capacity of 10 Tbit/s is achieved in C and L bands at a record 1.28 bit/s/Hz spectral efficiency.

articleTitle: Impact of nonlinear pump interactions on broadband distributed Raman amplification
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: Broadband distributed Raman amplification is helpful in multi-terabit transmission experiments requiring high and flat gains over a wide spectral window. We show that nonlinear pump interactions can severely degrade amplifier performance at high pump powers.

articleTitle: Compensation of chromatic dispersion and dispersion slope using a virtually imaged phased array
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: Chromatic dispersion produced by the virtually imaged phased array (VIPA) is discussed. A newly designed 3-dimensional mirror produces uniform dispersion for each WDM channel with a wide variable dispersion range. The VIPA with the mirror also produces dispersion slope by including a diffraction grating.

articleTitle: Electronic PMD mitigation-from linear equalization to maximum-likelihood detection
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: In a comparative study post-detection signal processing performed by transversal-filter, decision-feedback-equalizer, the concatenation of both, or maximum-likelihood sequence detection is analyzed for PMD penalty reduction. Optical noise sources and second-order PMD are taken into account.

articleTitle: A highly integrated 32-SOA gates optoelectronic module suitable for IP multi-terabit optical packet routers
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: For the first time, the realization and the performance of a compact optoelectronic 32-SOA module including their drivers is reported. Preliminary experiments in an optical packet switching matrix for IP multi-terabit router is also reported.

articleTitle: Novel RZ signal format with alternate-chirp for suppression of nonlinear degradation in 40 Gb/s based WDM
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: A novel alternate-chirped RZ signal format is proposed. 2 dB improvement in nonlinear tolerance has been confirmed experimentally, compared to CS-RZ format in 40 Gb/s based WDM-480 km transmission experiment with 100-GHz channel spacing.

articleTitle: Compact integrated tunable chromatic dispersion compensator with a 4000 ps/nm tuning range
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: A +/-2000 ps/nm continuous tuning range with low group delay ripple was demonstrated for 10 Gb/s NRZ signals using ring resonator allpass filters with diameters of 2 mm in silica-on-silicon planar waveguides.

articleTitle: Wavelength routing based on physical impairments
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: A set of guidelines for routing wavelengths in switched optical networks that is based on physical constraints is presented. Impact on signaling protocols is also discussed. One may still choose to break down the automatically switched optical network (ASON) into multiple sub-networks, but the choice will now be based on administrative or business considerations rather than physical constraints. Hence, we shall concentrate on the methods that may be employed in estimating the quality of service for a transparent wavelength connection through such an ASON.

articleTitle: Demonstration of adaptive PMD compensation at 40 Gb/s
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We report for the first time the full experimental assessment of an adaptive PMD compensator at 40 Gb/s over realistic PMD statistics. Results, consolidated by numerical simulations, show that the PMD limit is raised from 4 to 8 ps with the compensator.

articleTitle: 1480-1510 nm-band Tm doped fiber amplifier (TDFA) with a high power conversion efficiency of 42 %
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: The highest reported power conversion efficiency of 42 % has been achieved using a high Tm/sup 3+/ concentration doped fluoride fiber amplifier with one color 1.4 /spl mu/m pumping and a double pass configuration for S-band amplification. We achieved gains exceeding 26 dB and NFs of less than 7 dB in the 1480 to 1510 nm wavelength region (30 nm bandwidth). Furthermore, an 8 /spl times/ 10 Gb/s transmission experiment clarified that there was no excess noise generated in our proposed gain-shifted GS-TDFAs.

articleTitle: All-optical packet routing by an out-of-band optical label and wavelength conversion in a full-mesh network based on a cyclic-frequency AWG
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We demonstrate all-optical packet routing using an out-of-band optical label and wavelength conversion in a cyclic-frequency arrayed-waveguide grating (AWG) based full-mesh network with shared multiple light sources. Gigabit Ethernet packets were successfully routed using our technique.

articleTitle: Widely tunable external cavity diode laser based on a MEMS electrostatic rotary actuator
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: A C-band continuously tunable external cavity diode laser based on a MEMS electrostatic rotary actuator provides 15 ms tuning time with +7 dBm output power across a 40 nm tuning range and 55 dB side mode suppression.

articleTitle: Bi-criteria studies of mesh network restoration path-length versus capacity tradeoffs
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: Mesh-restorable networks are of interest as an alternative to rings for DWDM-based optical networks. We study the capacity design of mesh networks using a bi-criteria formulation to explore the optimal trade-off between restoration capacity and restoration path lengths.

articleTitle: A quantum-limited optically-matched communication link
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We propose and demonstrate a nearly optimum all-optically matched communication link with unsurpassed receiver sensitivities better than 0.5 dB from quantum-limited performance at 5 Gbps using an approach that can be extended to higher data rates. We have demonstrated record optical communication performance, less than 0.5 dB from quantum limited theory for optically preamplified OOK.

articleTitle: Fundamental noise limits in broadband Raman amplifiers
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We show that broadband discrete Raman amplifiers based on silica-germania will have a noise figure significantly greater than the quantum limit. We also present temperature measurements on a broadband distributed Raman amplifier using asymmetrically-spaced pumps.

articleTitle: A short recirculating fiber loop testbed with accurate reproduction of Maxwellian PMD statistics
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: A short recirculating fiber loop (/spl sim/100 km) that can emulate polarisation mode dispersion (PMD) with Maxwellian statistics is realized by loop-synchronous polarization scrambling inside the loop. The performance of our distribution-correct PMD loop is. compared both experimentally and numerically to that of a distribution-incorrect PMD loop.

articleTitle: A comparison study between slotted and unslotted all-optical packet-switched network with priority-based routing
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We present a comparison between a slotted and unslotted all-optical packet-switched network with priority-based routing. Packet loss rate below 0.01 with transmitter load less than 0.3 in the unslotted network is achieved by using buffering, limited wavelength conversion and deflection. OCIS codes: (060.4250) Networks.

articleTitle: Comparison of centralized and distributed provisioning of lightpaths in optical networks
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: This paper compares centralized and distributed online provisioning approaches in optical networks. In the centralized approach, complete network state is available for path computation. In the distributed approach, summarized information is available for path computation.

articleTitle: Novel architecture of wavelength interleaving filter with Fourier transform-based MZIs
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: A novel wavelength interleaving filter (interleaver) has been demonstrated with Fourier transform-based Mach Zehnder interferometers (MZIs). The interleaver works as two independent 1/spl times/2 interleavers by sharing their delay lines and couplers.

articleTitle: Wavelength multicasting using an ultra high-speed all-optical wavelength converter
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: A new multicasting scheme based on 1 to 8-wavelength conversion is proposed for future high-speed broadband networks. 40 Gbit/s optical time domain multiplexed (OTDM) data was used to simultaneously impose phase modulation on 4 CW channels, 3.6 nm apart. The resulting sidebands were filtered using an arrayed waveguide router (AWGR) to obtain 8 different 40 Gbit/s OTDM channels. The measured bit-error rates indicate a power penalty of less than 1.5 dB.

articleTitle: Monolithic widely-tunable DBR lasers
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: Tunable lasers are poised to dominate most applications areas within the next few years. Widely-tunable monolithic DBR lasers have the capability to satisfy the requirements of nearly every application area. This presentation will describe the activities to realize this goal.

articleTitle: 400-channel 25-GHz spacing arrayed-waveguide grating covering a full range of C- and L-bands
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We realized a 400-channel 25-GHz spacing arrayed-waveguide (AWG) on a 6-inch Si wafer using 1.5%-/spl Delta/ silica-based waveguides. This AWG covers the full C- and L-bands and exhibits an on-chip loss of 3.8-6.4 dB.

articleTitle: Enhanced PMD mitigation by polarization scrambling and forward error correction
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We propose a new fibre polarization mode dispersion (PMD) mitigation scheme that combines polarization scrambling with forward error correction and adaptive electronic equalization. Simulations demonstrate that the remaining power penalties are significantly reduced.

articleTitle: 48 % power conversion efficiency in a single-pump gain-shifted thulium-doped fiber amplifier
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: A new pumping scheme (1.2 /spl mu/m+1.4 /spl mu/m) is demonstrated for the gain-shifted TDFA, leading to record efficiency of 48% using one single pump dual-wavelength laser. This pumping scheme was implemented with a dual wavelength Raman fiber laser, giving 48% optical efficiency.

articleTitle: Dynamic dispersion, compensation devices for high speed transmission systems
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: Dynamic dispersion compensation technologies are becoming paramount in high-speed WDM lightwave systems, operating at per-channel bit-rates of 40Gb/s and above. Tunable dispersion can extend transmission distances, mitigate nonlinear effects, and improve systems margins. The paper reviews a number of emerging technologies and considers system performance issues.

articleTitle: Protection path routing on WDM networks
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: An important design issue in protection path routing lies in utilizing the wavelength sharing potential presented by non-concurrent failure events. We propose a novel routing algorithm that aim to maximally exploits these sharing opportunities.

articleTitle: An improved OSNR monitoring technique based on polarization-nulling method
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We report on the improved OSNR monitoring technique for WDM networks using the polarization-nulling method. Unlike the previous techniques based on the polarization, the proposed technique was not sensitive to PMD and nonlinear birefringence.

articleTitle: Fast adaptive control for electronic equalization of PMD
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We propose an adaptive control scheme, based on the least mean squares algorithm, for electronic equalization of polarization mode dispersion. Fast adaptation is demonstrated by numerical simulations and experiments at 10 Gb/s.

articleTitle: S-band amplification in a thulium doped silicate fiber
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We demonstrate significant gain over 1470-1540 nm in a thulium doped silica fiber amplifier. The fiber is compatible with standard fabrication techniques, and can be fusion spliced to standard telecommunications fibers. we report the first demonstration of an S-band thulium doped fiber amplifier (TDFA) using a true silicate fiber host which is readily spliced to standard fibers and compatible with standard fabrication technologies. Modifications in composition are expected to yield improvements in lifetime which may enable a truly practical TDFA.

articleTitle: Higher order polarization mode dispersion compensator with three degrees of freedom
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We compare several PMD compensation methods, and find that the simple PMD compensator with a variable polarization controller (PC) and a variable time delay line can compensate for not only first, but also higher order PMD.

articleTitle: High spectral efficiency (0.53 bit/s/Hz) WDM transmission of 160 Gb/s per wavelength over 400 km of fiber
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: A spectral efficiency of 0.53 b/s/Hz is demonstrated at 160 Gb/s over 400 km. The pseudo-linear transmission regime with 100% post compensation is used, and the transmission loss through the 100 km spans is compensated with distributed Raman amplification only.

articleTitle: Architectures and algorithm for multicasting in WDM optical mesh networks using opaque and transparent optical cross-connects
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: As the WDM technology grows, multicast applications will become widely popular. In the study, we present two kinds of switch architectures to support multicasting. We present preliminary results obtained for efficient routing and wavelength assignment (RWA) of multicast sessions.

articleTitle: All-optical clock recovery for 3R optical regeneration
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: Scalable all-optical networks need 3R regeneration. Clock recovery is a key function. Bit-rate flexibility and ultrafast locking are important in future asynchronous Internet protocol (IP) networks. The performance of regenerators is demonstrated in loop experiments.

articleTitle: Novel hole-assisted lightguide fiber exhibiting large anomalous dispersion and low loss below 1 dB/km
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We propose a novel holed fiber based on lightguiding by glass index difference and dispersion enhancement by holes. Due to the reduced power fraction in the holes, a record-breaking low loss of 0.82 dB/km at 1550 nm is achieved with extraordinarily large anomalous dispersion of +34 ps/nm/km.

articleTitle: Experiments in fast restoration using GMPLS in optical/electronic mesh networks
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We present experimental results demonstrating that generalised multi-protocol label switching (GMPLS) with resource reservation protocol (RSVP) can be applied to optical/electrical mesh networks to yield ultra-fast provisioning and restoration times competitive with SONET rings, confirming results previously predicted by simulation.

articleTitle: Limitations to first-order PMD compensation in WDM systems due to XPM-induced PSP changes
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We show both numerically and experimentally that the nonlinear phase change due to cross-phase modulation (XPM) induces a bit-pattern-dependent change in the state-of-polarization that translates to uncertainty in the principal states of polarization (PSP). This effect severely limits the effectiveness of first-order polarization mode dispersion (PMD) post-compensation and suggests the use of in-line compensation.

articleTitle: The potential of optical layer networks
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: There is enormous potential in newly emerging optical layer networks that support a rapidly growing Internet backbone. This potential stems from the value of extended reach to remove costly regenerators, the value of configurability to reduce provisioning times between IP routers, and the value of optical peering to increase the efficiency of the EP backbone network.

articleTitle: SLSP: a new path protection scheme for the optical Internet
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: The Short Leap Shared Protection (SLSP) is a new scheme for end-to-end path protection for the optical Internet. The paper presents the design and operation of SLSP in MPLS-based optical networks.

articleTitle: Integrated 10 Gb/s chirped return-to-zero transmitter using GaAs-AlGaAs modulators
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: A four-stage integrated module for 10 Gb/s chirped return-to-zero modulation is realized using GaAs-AlGaAs electro-optic guided-wave technology. Performance is verified by dispersion-managed test bed transmission over 3000 km.

articleTitle: Quantifying the benefits of selective wavelength regeneration in ultra long-haul WDM networks
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: Investigates the performance of transparent OXCs exploiting selective wavelength regeneration for different maximum transparency lengths. The results reveal the tradeoff between increased transparency length and reduced cost assigned to O/E/O regeneration.

articleTitle: Extending the L-band to 1620 nm using MCS fiber
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: Compositional modifications to the base MCS (antimony silicate) glass composition permit extension of useable L-band gain from 1615 to 1620 nm. This is achieved by shifting the signal excited state absorption band to longer wavelengths.

articleTitle: PLZT electro-optic waveguides and switches
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: Switches using (Pb,La)(Zr,Ti)O/sub 3/ waveguides on Nb-doped SrTiO/sub 3/ semiconductor substrates were fabricated. A fabricated 1 2 switch showed crosstalk of n22 dB and response of 20 ns at a voltage as low as 10 V.

articleTitle: High-power and high-efficiency photodiode with an evanescently coupled graded-index waveguide for 40 Gb/s applications
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: High-power evanescently coupled pin photodiodes with external efficiencies of as high as 0.96 A/W, enabled by the graded index configuration of the waveguide, have been developed for 40 Gb/s applications.

articleTitle: Non-Maxwellian DGD distributions of PMD emulators
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We use importance sampling to determine the differential group delay probability distribution produced by various polarization-mode-dispersion emulator models, showing that the tail probabilities can be orders of magnitude smaller than best-fit Maxwellian distributions. PMD emulators can therefore significantly underestimate the probability of rare DGD events.

articleTitle: A widely tunable fiber Bragg grating with a wavelength tunability over 40 nm
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We have fabricated and demonstrated a 40 nm widely tunable fiber Bragg grating designed for operation over erbium band. This device is simple, low-cost and will have great potential for applications in optical communication and sensing.

articleTitle: All-optical nonblocking terabit/s crossconnect based on low power all-optical wavelength converter and MEMS switch fabric
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: All-optical nonblocking routing of 80 10 Gb/s C-band channels is demonstrated with a 100/spl times/100 optical crossconnect. The enabling technology is a channel equalizing low-power wavelength converter operating with -14 dBm input power such that no single channel amplification is needed.

articleTitle: Variable optical attenuator with large dynamic range and low drive power
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We demonstrate a polymer waveguide-based thermo-optic variable optical attenuator with 30dB dynamic range that requires only 10mW of drive power at 30dB. The design offers low insertion loss (<1.0dB) and is compatible with planar processing.

articleTitle: 2.4 Tb/s (120 /spl times/ 20 Gb/s) transmission over transoceanic distance using optimum FEC overhead and 48 % spectral efficiency
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We have demonstrated 2.4 Tb/s (120 /spl times/ 20 Gb/s) transmission over the transoceanic distance of 6,200 km using optimum forward error correction (FEC) code overhead, 48% spectral efficiency, ultra-low slope dispersion map, and full C-band EDFAs.

articleTitle: Influence of PMD on the performance of optical transmission systems in the presence of PDL
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: Polarization dependent loss and polarization mode dispersion have been treated as separate phenomena in optical transmission systems. Simulation results indicate significant penalties from interaction of these effects, which must be considered in system design.

articleTitle: Performance improvement of highly nonlinear long-distance optical fiber transmission system using novel high gain forward error correcting code
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: Performance improvement of long-distance optical fiber transmission system with novel high gain forward error correcting code is presented. This new code realizes both moderate nonlinear transmission impairment and high coding gain.

articleTitle: Wavelength usage efficiency versus recovery time in path-protected DWDM mesh networks
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We describe novel lightpath routing and protection schemes and demonstrate an inverse relationship between efficiency of wavelength usage and restoration time. The methodology is used in the selection of grade of protection in all-optical networks.

articleTitle: Analysis of polarization-mode dispersion compensators using importance sampling
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We use importance sampling to analyze polarization-mode dispersion (PMD) compensators that consist of a single differential-group delay (DGD) element. Using this technique we show that while these compensators improve the average penalty due to PMD, they may degrade the outage probability.

articleTitle: Broadband discrete fiber Raman amplifier with high differential gain operating over 1.65 μm-band
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: A high differential-gain (0.08 dB/mW), low-noise ( < 5.0 dB), broadband (30 nm) and flat-gain ( < ±1 dB) fiber Raman amplifier operating over the 1.65 μm-band has been demonstrated employing a low-loss highly nonlinear fiber and a broadened pump light source.

articleTitle: MEMS electrostatic actuators for optical switching applications
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: Electrostatic actuators providing linear and angular deflection have been developed using deep reactive ion etching (DRIE). Optical switches with 0.5 dB loss at 1550 nm have been made showing switching times less than 5 ms.

articleTitle: Influence of the dispersion map on limitations due to cross-phase modulation in WDM multispan transmission systems
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We determine system limitations due to cross-phase modulation (XPM) for non-zero dispersion shifted fiber by experiments and simulations. For the worst case of full dispersion compensation in each span we find a maximum power law whereas for appropriate undercompensation XPM can be efficiently suppressed.

articleTitle: 10 Gb/s SCM system using optical single side-band modulation
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: A 10 Gb/s subcarrier multiplexing (SCM) long-haul optical system is reported. 4/spl times/2.5 Gb/s data streams are combined into one wavelength, which occupies a 20 GHz optical bandwidth. Optical single sideband modulation (SSB) is used to increase bandwidth efficiency and reduce dispersion penalty.

articleTitle: Demonstration of data remodulation for upstream traffic in WDM access networks using injection-locked FP laser as modulator
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We propose and demonstrate an upstream-traffic remodulation scheme based on injection locking of a FP laser diode on the downstream wavelength. The original 10 Gbit/s downstream data are largely suppressed, allowing simultaneous direct modulation of 1-Gb/s upstream data with improved signal quality.

articleTitle: MEMS-based photonic switching in communications networks
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: All optical or photonic switching is key to the next-generation intelligent optical networks. It enables rapid dynamic provisioning, protection and restoration of network connections cost-effectively, which support revenue-generating services including bandwidth on demand and DWDM over IP. In the past 12 months, MEMS-based photonic cross connect switches have gone from the lab to commercial availability and are now in carrier field trials. Photonic switching is inherently capable of transparently. switching any bit rate and data format. Optical MEMS enables switching any transmission wavelength, or wavelength band in a scalable, reliable, low power, compact size providing flexible solutions to the bandwidth demands of long haul, metro, and access networks. This paper will discuss MEMS based photonic switching subsystems and their commercial deployment.

articleTitle: Chromatic and polarization mode dispersion measurement technique using phase-sensitive sideband detection
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: A new technique for measuring chromatic dispersion and PMD is presented that does not require a tunable laser. To demonstrate the technique, measurements on a fiber Bragg grating are compared to the modulation phase-shift method. The widely used modulation phase-shift technique for chromatic dispersion measurement utilizes a double sideband modulated signal and a swept carrier frequency to measure delay. The sidebands must have the same amplitude, and the change in delay and frequency must be accurately measured to obtain the dispersion. In the new technique, phase-sensitive detection is performed for each sideband individually.

articleTitle: Simple and fast method for step size determination in computations of signal propagation through nonlinear fibres
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: Presents a simple and fast method for determination of the step size that exactly leads to a prescribed accuracy when signal propagation through nonlinear optical fibres is computed using the split-step Fourier method.

articleTitle: 300 Gbit/s eye-diagram measurement by optical sampling using fiber based parametric amplification
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: 300 Gbit/s optical signal eye-diagram measurements have been demonstrated for the first time by all-optical sampling using parametric amplification in a highly nonlinear fiber with a resolution of 1.6 ps. The measured eye-diagrams are updated in real-time.

articleTitle: Performance limit of forward error correction codes in optical fiber communications
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We investigate performance limits of forward error correction codes in optically-amplified fiber channels with asymmetric channel statistics. We show that the binary symmetric channel approximation underestimates the maximum coding gain achievable in fiber communications.

articleTitle: Dispersion and dispersion-slope correction with a fiber Bragg grating over the full C-band
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: Long-length wide-bandwidth fiber Bragg gratings for use as dispersion compensators that cover the full C-band have been fabricated. These devices are shown to work well in a 10 Gbit/s NRZ optical communications system.

articleTitle: 50 GHz spacing, multi-wavelength tunable locker integrated in a transmitter module with a monolithic-modulator and a DFB-laser
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: 50-GHz-spacing multi-wavelength-locker was developed. It consists of a temperature-compensated Fabry-Perot-etalon integrated in a transmitter-module with a monolithic-modulator and a DFB-laser. Its locking-accuracy is less than +/-10-pm and capture-range is more than +/-0.12-nm.

articleTitle: All-fiber acousto-optic tunable bandpass filter
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We report a novel, 3.5 nm bandpass, zero frequency shift, all-fiber AOTF employing a single acoustic flexural wave to couple light from the core mode to a cladding mode (propagating past a core block) and back again to the core mode.

articleTitle: Challenges of 40 Gb/s WDM transmission
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: In addition to the required high-bandwidth electronics, wavelength-division-multiplexed 40 Gb/s transmission faces a number of challenges including optical-signal-to-noise ratio, dispersion and dispersion slope, and polarization mode dispersion. We discuss these issues as well as polarization multiplexing, a potential technique to achieve 0.8 bit/s/Hz spectral efficiency.

articleTitle: Impact of filter concatenation on the performance of metropolitan area optical networks utilizing directly modulated lasers
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: In this work we study experimentally (using a re-circulating loop) and theoretically (using Q-factor calculations) the impact of the different chirp characteristics of 2.5Gb/s directly modulated lasers on the filter concatenation effects in transparent metropolitan area optical networks.

articleTitle: Dispersion-free fibre Bragg gratings
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: Fibre Bragg gratings with reduced/eliminated in-band dispersion are presented. When tested in add-drop configurations at 10 Gbit/s both 25 GHz and 50 GHz bandwidth gratings are shown to exhibit superior performance with no dispersion-induced penalties in the stopband. Furthermore, the demonstrated linear-phase Bragg gratings have >70% channel filling factor values and reflectivities in excess of 99.9%.

articleTitle: Widely tunable twin fiber grating dispersion compensator for 80 Gbit/s
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: The dispersion tolerance of an 80 Gbit/s system is broadened 27-fold, from 32.7 ps/nm to 884.9 ps/nm, using an adjustable dispersion compensator with novel grating design. This is the largest reported broadening of any system.

articleTitle: 1.25 Gbit/s transmission of optical FFH-OCDMA signals over 80 km with 16 users
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: Encoding/decoding of FFH-OCDMA signals from 16 users is performed with Bragg grating arrays. Transmission of the multiplexed signals is demonstrated over 80 km of standard fiber at data rate exceeding 1 Gbit/s using dispersion compensating modules.

articleTitle: Optical-label switching and routing by rapidly tunable wavelength conversion and uniform loss cyclic frequency array-waveguide grating
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We experimentally demonstrate optical-label switching and routing by combining rapidly tunable wavelength conversion with an arrayed waveguide grating router. The subcarrier optical-label content was optically extracted and processed, which induced forwarding decision and optical routing with a new label content.

articleTitle: A high SNR, 150 ch supercontinuum CW optical source with precise 25 GHz spacing for 10 Gbit/s DWDM systems
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: A 150 channel multi-wavelength CW optical source with precise 25 GHz spacing is successfully realized by longitudinal mode slicing of a supercontinuum spectrum. We confirm the generation of more than 150 CW channels ranging from 1530 to 1560 nm with SNRs over 28.2 dB and Q-factors over 20.8 dB which are sufficient for 10 Gbit/s multi-span DWDM transmission.

articleTitle: Thulium-doped tellurite glasses for S-band amplification
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: The advantages of tellurite glass hosts for Tm-doped S-band gain media are investigated. Comparisons are made with fluoride hosts and the ability to control bandwidth. by choice of tellurite glass composition is demonstrated.

articleTitle: Group delay reference artifact based on molecular gas absorption
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We propose a novel group delay reference for optical communication systems based on a molecular gas cell absorption characteristic. A 1.53 /spl mu/m C/sub 2/H/sub 2/ acetylene gas absorption cell commonly used as a wavelength reference is shown to have an important dispersive nature that forms the basis of a novel group delay reference. Group delay measurements are compared to theoretical predictions based on the amplitude response of the molecular gas cell. The formulated analytical approach is applicable to an arbitrary absorption spectra described by a Lorentzian function.

articleTitle: IP Ethernet versus ATM: the case for IP in the local loop
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: This paper explains why next generation local access networks will evolve to an all-optical IP Ethernet architecture that supports quality of service and management for a full range of voice, data and video services.

articleTitle: Optical layer shared protection using an IP-based optical control network
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: A novel approach to optical layer shared protection of optical networks using strictly Internet Protocol-based network controllers is presented. A protection time of /spl sim/15ms is measured for a 5-node optical network.

articleTitle: Polarisation dependence and gain tilt of Raman amplifiers for WDM systems
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We investigate the polarisation dependence and gain tilt of Raman amplifiers for WDM systems. We find no polarisation dependence of the gain for backward propagating pumps. Results from experiments on commercial 32 -channel WDM system are presented, highlighting the effect of gain tilt and pump depletion.

articleTitle: CW, multiple wavelength, room temperature, Raman fiber ring laser with external 19 channel, 10GHz pulse generation in a single electro-absorption modulator
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: Simultaneous CW generation of over 24 wavelength channels with 100GHz spacing at 1550 nm has been demonstrated at room temperature in a Raman ring laser with Fabry-Perot. A single EAM was employed to simultaneously modulate 19 of the output channels at 10GHz.

articleTitle: Cost-effective metro WDM network architectures
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: Various architecture options for the metropolitan network are evaluated. A novel passive optical routing WDM architecture is presented and shown to offer significant cost advantages with increasing network traffic requirements.

articleTitle: Vestigial side band demultiplexing for ultra high capacity (0.64 bit/s/Hz) transmission of 128/spl times/40 Gb/s channels
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: Vestigial sideband filtering with high crosstalk suppression is demonstrated as optical demux of densely packed 40 Gb/s channels with high spectral efficiency of 0.64 bit/s/Hz. Narrow band optical filters have been applied for separation of 128/spl times/40 Gbit/s channels with alternating spacings of 50 and 75 GHz.

articleTitle: Comparison of CRZ, RZ and NRZ modulation formats in a 64 /spl times/ 12.3 Gb/s WDM transmission experiment over 9000 km
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We present a comparison of CRZ, RZ and NRZ modulation formats in a 64 /spl times/ 12.3 Gb/s WDM transmission experiment up to 9000 km. We show that CRZ exhibits the strongest resistance to nonlinear propagation effects and is thus the most suitable format for high-capacity long-haul WDM systems.

articleTitle: Designing survivable networks using effective routing and wavelength assignment (RWA)
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: Electronic layers use primary and backup paths for protection. With WDM both may traverse the same physical link and fail simultaneously.

articleTitle: Addressing transparency in DWDM mesh survivable networks
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We identify the penalties incurred in all-optical networks on routing and restoration operations. We show that these penalties can be avoided with opaque switches interfaced by transponders. we demonstrate that transparent OXCs may be short of important functionality, and usability necessary to build robust and cost-effective networks. We arrive at our conclusion mainly by quantifying the amount of resources required to accommodate predefined OC48 traffic forecasts in the proposed architectures. We show that carriers opting for all-optical solutions will have to over build their infrastructures and surmount tremendous management obstacles in order to be competitive.

articleTitle: Dispersion monitoring and compensation using a single inband subcarrier tone
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We demonstrate a simple technique for dispersion monitoring by adding a single inband tone to the data. Our technique has high accuracy and an easily reconfigurable measurement range. Dispersion compensation is also demonstrated using the monitor's output.

articleTitle: Measurement of polarization mode dispersion based on optical frequency domain reflectometry technique
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: A new method for measurement of polarization mode dispersion in optical fibers based on optical frequency domain reflectometry technology is proposed and demonstrated with the use of a frequency-shifted feedback fiber laser as light source.

articleTitle: Reliable quality of transport monitoring in optical transparent paths of all-optical DWDM-networks
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: A method for monitoring the quality of optical transport services is introduced. Using spread spectrum technology leads to least interferring to payload. The method's performance and laboratory measurements are presented in this paper. This paper introduces a novel method for permanent online measurment of path characteristics. The measurement method does not interfere with the payload and also does not rely to it. It enables network providers to supervise the quality of transport through any optical transparent path.

articleTitle: Demonstration of 2-D plastic optical fibre based optical interconnect between CMOS ICs
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: The design and fabrication of a digital system demonstrator implementing 2D optical interconnect via a POF ribbon are discussed. This demonstrator implements 256 optical I/O channels per chip. Each chip, a custom FPGA CMOS design, implements digital and analogue functionality.

articleTitle: Fiber-effective-area managed fiber lines with distributed Raman amplification in 1.28=Tb/s (32/spl times/40 gb/s), 202-km unrepeatered transmission
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We propose the fiber-effective-area managed distributed Raman amplification system. The proposed transmission line enabled 1 dB improvement of the optical signal-to-noise-ratio and Q value so that 32/spl times/40 Gb/s WDM unrepeatered transmission of 202-km was achieved.

articleTitle: Outage probability of high speed transmission systems: the impact of PMD in comparison to other disruptive effects
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: The PMD tolerance of 10 Gbit/s transmission systems is calculated for a given DGD tolerance. The unavailability of the transmission system due to PMD is chosen relatively to the unavailability caused by other disruptive effects.

articleTitle: FWM resonances in dispersion slope-matched and non-zero-dispersion fiber maps: impact on system performance
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We show that FWM resonances can affect performance of selected channels within the DWDM band. These resonances could cause a Q-factor penalty in excess of 1 dB. Dispersion slope-matched maps and manufacturing variations help to suppress the resonances.

articleTitle: Optical control of rational harmonic mode-locking in a fiber laser for bright and dark pulse generation
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: Rational harmonic mode-locking is first demonstrated in an erbium-doped fiber laser using an all-optical approach. The setup provides a means for the conversion of wavelength, as well as the conversion between bright and dark pulses.

articleTitle: Reducing PMD impairments
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We review the optical and electrical PMD compensation schemes that can be found in the literature. Because of the statistical nature of PMD, most of them are composed of an adaptive counteractive element, a feedback signal and a tracking algorithm. We also mention the importance of PMD statistics emulation and of the long-term field experiments related to PMD.

articleTitle: Cancellation of spectral spread by pump frequency modulation in optical fiber wavelength converter
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We propose a novel highly-efficient wavelength conversion technique based on the four-wave mixing in the optical fiber, which can suppress not only the stimulated Brillouin scattering but also the spread of the converted spectrum. We proposed and demonstrated a novel highly efficient wavelength conversion technique without spectral spread of the converted signal, in which frequency of pump light and phase of signal light are modulated synchronously. The experimental setup proved our scheme to be effective for highly efficient wavelength conversion without spectral spread.

articleTitle: Improvement of switching time in a thermocapillarity optical switch
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: A switching time of 6 ms is achieved in a thermocapillarity switch by lowering the viscosity of the refractive-index-matching oil and improving the switch design. Further improvements would result in sub-ms switching time in this switch.

articleTitle: Fiber laser with repetition rate stabilization by semiconductor saturable absorber in CPM configuration
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: Fabry-Perot semiconductor saturable absorber has been implemented in a colliding pulse configuration for stabilizing a harmonically mode-locked fiber laser. An environmentally stable colliding-pulse mode-locked (CPM) design is shown to enhance supermode suppression.

articleTitle: Simultaneous multi-channel PMD equalization for WDM systems
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We confirmed a simultaneous multi-channel PMD equalization scheme for WDM channels by simulation, which consists of a variable lattice optical circuit, WDM-DMUX, channel PMD monitors. The steepest-descent method shows successful multi-channel PMD equalization.

articleTitle: Measurement of the polarization coupling length in telecom fibers using nonlinear polarization rotation
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: The polarization coupling length, an important parameter of the PMD probability distribution, is obtained from measurements and modeling of the nonlinear polarization rotation in optical fibers. Results for different types of fibers are presented.

articleTitle: All-fiber polarization monitoring and system applications
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: This paper discusses the advantages and recent progress in all-fiber polarization monitoring and the applications of this technology to all-optical WDM system applications. Recently demonstrated all-fiber polarimeters show promise of providing low-cost, compact, in-line polarization monitoring. The availability of such devices may enable WDM system applications such as ail-optical, bit-rate independent PMD mitigation and polarization demultiplexing.

articleTitle: Optimisation of polyphase concatenated arrayed-waveguide grating designs for 40 Gb/s adaptive dispersion compensation
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We describe the optimised polyphase addition of concatenated adaptive chirped arrayed-waveguide grating dispersion characteristics to produce up to /spl plusmn/210 ps/nm in-line dispersion compensation for all 40 Gb/s channels across the 100 GHz-ITU-grid with just /spl plusmn/7.4 ps/nm residual ripple.

articleTitle: Message encoding/decoding using chaotic pulsing semiconductor lasers
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: Chaotic communication using chaotic pulsing semiconductor lasers has been investigated. A high-speed digital message has been encoded/decoded on a chaotic pulsing carrier. Good message hiding during transmission and message recovery at a receiver has been observed.

articleTitle: Analysis of reconfiguration in IP over WDM access networks
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: The benefit/cost tradeoff of reconfiguration in IP/WDM networks is evaluated as the resulting reduction in average packet delay. We compare, analytically and through simulations, the performance of several reconfiguration policies to fixed topology systems. We develop a queuing model for a reconfigurable network that allows us to directly quantify the benefits and costs of reconfiguration as the resulting average packet delay. This simple model allows us to compare, both analytically and via simulations, appropriate reconfiguration policies and to determine the network reconfiguration downtime that can be tolerated.

articleTitle: Dispersive frequency multiplication for wavelength-tunable high repetition rate pulse-train generation
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We describe a simple method for generating wavelength-tunable pulses by optically-modulating the gain of an SOA in a ring-laser with frequency multiplied pulse-train. Wavelength-tunable pulses at repetition rates of 20, 30 or 40 GHz were generated.

articleTitle: Silica-based 16 /spl times/ 16 optical matrix switch module with integrated driving circuits
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We fabricated a 16 /spl times/ 16 optical matrix switch module in which a silica-based thermooptic switch chip and driving circuits were integrated. Our use of serial interfaces allowed us to realize a practicable module with a simple structure.

articleTitle: Measurement of chromatic dispersion and length of optical fiber using a Sagnac interferometer employing an acousto-optic frequency-shifter
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: A technique for accurate measurement of the chromatic dispersion and length of single mode fiber is demonstrated using a novel Sagnac interferometer that employs an acousto-optic frequency-shifter. This requires no fast detection equipment and is suitable for measurement of installed fiber with tens of kilometers of length.

articleTitle: Demonstration of ultra-wideband and transparent virtual optical code/wavelength path network
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: Ultra-wideband (8.05 THz) and transparent virtual optical code/wavelength path network capable of optical code and wavelength conversion by supercontinuum generation with optical 3R is experimentally demonstrated with the total link lengths of 180 km at 10 Gbit/s.

articleTitle: Enhancement of supercontinuum spectrum generation due to cross-phase modulation in a dispersion-flattened/decreasing fiber
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: A flat and broad bandwidth of 350 nm at -20dB for supercontinuum spectrum of soliton pulses was theoretically found to be generated due to cross-phase modulation from a dispersion-flattened/decreasing fiber of 2.4 km length.

articleTitle: Calculation of non-Gaussian intensity and timing jitter statistics in optical regenerated systems
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We present analytical method to calculate non-Gaussian intensity and timing jitters statistics in optical communication systems. Using developed method we have calculated probability density function for optical regenerated soliton systems with in-line synchronous intensity modulation and filtering.

articleTitle: Optical pulse pattern recognition circuit based on an optical digital-to-analog converter on a planar lightwave circuit
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: A 4-bit optical digital-to-analog converter for use in optical pulse pattern recognition has been fabricated on a silica-based planar light-wave circuit. We successfully confirmed the recognition of various kinds of 4-bit pulse sequence at 10 Gb/s.

articleTitle: High power ASE-free tunable laser using a Sagnac ring interferometer within the external cavity
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: The use of a Sagnac ring interferometer within the external cavity of a tunable laser diode is described. This optical scheme provides an ASE-free output, without any reduction of the output power.

articleTitle: High sensitivity waveform measurement of 160 Gbit/s signal with optical sampling using quasi-phasematched mixing in LiNbO/sub 3/ waveguide
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: High efficiency (1.7/spl times/10/sup -2/W/sup -1/) waveform measurement is experimentally demonstrated using quasi-phasematched mixing in a LiNbO/sub 3/ waveguide. A 160 Gbit/s optical waveform is observed with temporal resolution of 3.6 ps.

articleTitle: Fast and accurate measurement of the dispersion of cascaded components
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We show that the dispersion of multiple cascaded components can be determined from a single low-coherence interferometric measurement. This measurement is not adversely affected by other components in the system, regardless of their wavelength reflection bands.

articleTitle: Performance optimization of chirped return-to-zero format in 10-Gb/s terrestrial transmission systems
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: The performance of the chirped return-to-zero format varies significantly with slight changes in the link dispersion. Penalty reduction from more than 8 dB to 3 dB has been demonstrated by either adjusting the chirp or using tunable dispersion compensation.

articleTitle: Homodyne crosstalk performance of reconfigurable optical add-drop multiplexers
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We compare the homodyne crosstalk performance of three reconfigurable optical add-drop multiplexers. We find different statistical distributions of power penalty for each structure. These distributions depend on network size and capacity, indicating that different structures are more appropriate for different network applications.

articleTitle: Highly reliable 40 Gb/s electroabsorption modulator grown on InP:Fe substrate
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: An electroabsorption modulator with unburied ridge waveguide has been fabricated on InP:Fe substrate. The cut-off frequency was 40 GHz and the extinction ratio was 15 dB. The estimated lifetime at 25/spl deg/C was over 1.7/spl times/10/sup 7/ hours.

articleTitle: Ultrashort pulse switching in a lossy acousto-optic tunable filter (AOTF)
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: In this paper, we did a study of the transmission characteristics of the AOTF operating with ultrashort light pulses(2 ps). Initially one consider the performance of the device, operating in the nonlinear regime without loss. It was observed that the effect of dispersion and nonlinearity, has strong influence on the pulse propagation when one increase the length of the AOTF. For shorter length of the device the switched pulse is presenting time broadening. For higher length of the device, pulse breakup was observed. Considering the AOTF with loss one consider the device of length 0.25 mm with loss of 4 dB/mm constructed with an increasing nonlinearity profile. It was observed that the increase of the nonlinearity lead the switched pulse from broadening to optical compression. One can say that one can, operate the AOTF in a configuration that one can avoid the pulse break up and have a switched pulse with a shorter time duration compared with the lossy AOTF. The study of the AOTF operating with ultra short optical solitons provides possibilities for achieving, high efficiency in ultrafast all-optical signal processing, especially for optical switches, filters and Optical transistors.

articleTitle: Wavelength conversion based on cross-phase modulation in a semiconductor Mach-Zehnder modulator
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: Wavelength conversion based on cross-phase modulation in a reversely biased semiconductor Mach-Zehnder modulator is proposed and successfully demonstrated in a commercial device. The converted signals exhibit extinction ratio >13 dB and penalty <1.5 dB at 10 Gb/s for both NRZ and RZ formats.

articleTitle: Symmetry and birefringence in microstructured optical fibers
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: Symmetry prohibits birefringence in perfect photonic crystal fibers. Numerical methods not respecting symmetry require care in use. We present results in accord with symmetry arguments, using methods both respecting and breaking the fiber symmetry.

articleTitle: Optical filter responses of InGaAsP microdisk resonators fabricated by polymer wafer bonding
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: Optical filters based on InGaAsP microdisk resonators with 10 /spl mu/m and 5 /spl mu/m diameters have been fabricated using a polymer wafer bonding process. A narrow linewidth of 0.22 nm and large free spectral range of 38 nm near 1.55 /spl mu/m are obtained. These devices are potentially useful as wavelength add-drop filters in DWDM networks.

articleTitle: Shift and splitting of resonant peaks in long-period fiber gratings for sensing applications
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We also applied long period fibre gratings (LPFGs) to various sensing application such as bend, transverse load, and index change sensors by using the peak-splitting effect of LPFGs. Furthermore, since the lower order cladding mode is insensitive to the external perturbation change compared with the higher order cladding modes,We will discuss a simple method to change the transmission characteristics of long-period fiber gratings using UV post-exposure. Application of the resonant peak splitting to bend, transverse load, and index change sensing will be described.

articleTitle: Case study: live monitoring of a DWDM network
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: The description of a remote fiber test system (RFTS) featuring spectral analysis on a live DWDM system is presented. A project presentation is followed by descriptions of the network and on-site implementation, results analysis, and conclusion.

articleTitle: Dynamically flattened optical amplifiers
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: Summary form only given. Fixed gain flattening filters will be unable to meet the future requirements for amplifiers in high capacity systems. The range of possible designs and devices are reviewed, and the operational issues are examined.

articleTitle: Traffic grooming methods for undersea trunk and branch architectures
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: Undersea cable systems generally span many sovereign countries with variety of bandwidth needs. Trunk and branch arrangement provides a secure and cost-effective way of connecting these countries with a single cable system. However the cost per bandwidth mile of undersea cable systems is very high which makes efficient traffic grooming necessary. In this paper, we propose three grooming schemes in context of a trunk and branch network that deploys SDH ring transport to provide SDH pipes to carry PDH signals. The proposed methods are general and extend to other arrangements such as mesh-type transport and other signal levels.

articleTitle: Study of spatial-temporal characteristics of optical fiber based on ultra-short pulse interferometry
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We reconstruct modal intensity distribution for several spatial modes of optical fiber using autocorrelation of ultrashort pulses in Mach-Zehnder interferometer. The modes of optical fiber are separated in time due to group velocity dispersion, and detected experimentally by observing the interference of modal field distribution with time gating reference field.

articleTitle: Asymptotic analysis and design considerations of Bragg fibers
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: An asymptotic analysis is developed to calculate the modal dispersion, field distribution, and propagation loss of Bragg fibers. The design considerations of Bragg fibers are also discussed.

articleTitle: Vertically coupled GaAs-AlGaAs and GaInAsP-InP microring resonators
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: Single transverse mode vertically coupled semiconductor microring resonators were made using a novel fabrication technique without regrowth. GaAs-AlGaAs and GaInAsP-InP devices are demonstrated.

articleTitle: Comparison of photosensitivity in germanium doped silica fibers using 244 nm and 266 nm continuous-wave lasers
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
