abstract: Diode pumped continuous-wave UV lasers offer an interesting alternative to frequency doubled argon-ion lasers. We report the first photosensitivity comparison using these lasers on deuterium loaded standard telecommunication fibers and unloaded experimental fibers.

articleTitle: POF is overcoming silica in bit rate
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: The great advantage of the perfluorinated (PF) polymer base graded index polymer optical fiber ( GI POF) in bandwidth was clarified in detail. The PF polymer base POF has the potential of achieving the highest bit rate among existing physical media including even silica fiber, since the material dispersion of the PF polymer is lower than those of silica and other polymer materials. Therefore, more than 10 Gb/s bit rate transmission for 10giga Ethernet can be achieved by the POR. Campus LAN based on the PF polymer base GI POF has been actually installed in Keio University since last April. The system performance is briefly introduced in this paper.

articleTitle: L-band multi-wavelength erbium-doped fiber laser
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: A wideband multi-wavelength erbium-doped fiber laser in L-band with frequency shifted feedback and gain-loss balancing is presented. Laser channels with 400 GHz spacing over 20 nm bandwidth were demonstrated within 0.8 dB output power excursion.

articleTitle: Photon statistics of a single mode of spontaneous Raman scattering in a distributed Raman amplifier
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: Experimental measurement of spontaneous noise statistics from a distributed Raman amplifier has been achieved with single-mode and single-photon resolution. The results agree with quantum theoretical predictions of a Bose-Einstein probability distribution. Distributed Raman amplification is becoming increasingly important in today's optical communication systems. It improves the optical signal-to-noise ratio by providing optical gain inside the transmission fiber.

articleTitle: Increasing line rate by combining ETDM and OTDM in a semiconductor Mach-Zehnder modulator
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: Line rate is doubled by combining electrical time division multiplexing (ETDM) and OTDM techniques in a semiconductor Mach-Zehnder modulator. 20 Gb/s optical signal is successfully generated using a 10 GHz commercial module to multiplex two 10 Gb/s signals.

articleTitle: Technical challenges to multi-terabit transoceanic systems
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: Technical challenges to increase spectral efficiency and channel bit rate for multiterabit transoceanic systems are discussed. Feasibility of multi-terabit transmission using VSB-RZ format with high spectral efficiency of 0.6 bit/s/Hz and 40 Gbit/s WDM long distance transmission have been reviewed.

articleTitle: Reduced cross-talk semiconductor optical amplifiers based on type-II quantum wells
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: It is shown that using type-II QW active regions in SOA's will allow up to 10 dB reduction in the interchannel crosstalk at high (>2.5 Gbit/s) data rates. The reduction can be attained via a corresponding increase in saturation energy without any reduction in the efficiency.

articleTitle: Influence of dispersion properties of the delay line in self heterodyne linewidth measurements
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We report experimental results of the influence of 1/f noise on the laser linewidth measurements using the self heterodyne technique and suggest a method of isolating it from the dispersive broadening caused by the delay line in the interferometer.

articleTitle: Fabrication and numerical analysis of D-shaped optical fiber polarizer coated with chromium film
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: Fabrication process, numerical analysis, and optical properties of the D-shaped optical fiber coated with chromium film were studied. The D-shaped optical fiber was obtained by drawing the side-cut D-shaped preform made by MCVD process. The fiber polarizer was made by coating the flat side of the D-shaped optical fiber with chromium metal film and the maximum extinction ratio of the fiber polarizer was found to be about 55 dB.

articleTitle: Experimental investigation of collision-induced timing jitter and pulse distortion in WDM return-to-zero dispersion-managed systems
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: New pump-probe experiments quantify XPM-induced distortion in, dense WDM. RZ dispersion-managed transmission over standard fibre. Despite the collision-induced timing jitter, the use of appropriately dispersion-managed quasi-soliton pulses can extend transmission distances by a factor of 2 compared to NRZ-based systems.

articleTitle: High coupling in novel 2D-lattice distributed reflector laser gratings
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: It is shown that 2D lattice gratings, despite being placed outside the waveguide region, exhibit sufficiently strong coupling coefficients that optical modes rapidly. couple transversely into the etched grating region, yielding high coupling coefficients of 270 cm/sup -1/. This performance allows mode-hop-free lasing operation in DBR structures.

articleTitle: Versatile waveguide design for optical amplification
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: Optical amplification in novel rare-earth-doped waveguides is demonstrated. Design and measurements of an Erbium/Ytterbium co-doped glass waveguide amplifier are presented. The benefits of the design as applied to low-cost amplification are discussed.

articleTitle: Bi-directional photonic conversion between 4/spl times/10 Gbit/s OTDM and WDM by optical time-gating wavelength interchange
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: Novel photonic conversion and reconversion of 40 Gbit/s (4/spl times/10 Gbit/s) OTDM-to-WDM-to-OTDM by wavelength interchange using optical time-gating of highly chirped supercontinuum and high speed pulse trains are proposed and experimentally demonstrated.

articleTitle: Optical wavelength interchange based on nonlinear photonic crystals
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We have theoretically analyzed and experimentally demonstrated the first simultaneous optical wavelength interchange process using a two-dimensional nonlinear photonic crystal. Results from a 1535-1555 nm wavelength interchange lattice fabricated in lithium niobate will be presented.

articleTitle: Multi-purpose fiber-optic access network (MFAN)
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We propose and demonstrate a multi-purpose fiber-optic access network (MFAN). This network utilizes the same fiber infrastructure for a variety of services including baseband, CATV, PCS, WLL, and LMCS. The experimental results show that the proposed network could support the independent operation of these services.

articleTitle: Optical 3R regenerator based on Q-switched laser
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: A polarization and wavelength insensitive Q-switched laser is applied in a 3R regenerator experiment. The optical regenerator shows a negative power penalty of -2 dB at a data rate of 10 Gb/s RZ. The Q-switched laser offers a steep nonlinear all-optical transfer function. The optical 3R regenerator was tested with a degraded input signal.

articleTitle: Investments in optical networking - technological risks and opportunities
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: Optical component manufacturers, system vendors and broadband operators all attract a lot of investments. The paper address the technological risks and opportunities associated with these investments.

articleTitle: Group delay of a micro-optic dynamic gain-flattening filter
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We investigate the group delay spectrum of a novel micro-optic dynamic gain-flattening filter. We show theoretical delay of less than 1 ps over the operating range and compare with direct experimental measurements.

articleTitle: Experimental and theoretical study of crosstalk in WDM - CATV systems
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: Fiber nonlinearities are assessed theoretically and experimentally for WDM-CATV transmissions. For fixed channel number, twofold reduction of channel spacing or for fixed spacing, twofold increase of channel number, increases crosstalk by 3dB/ch and 1dB/ch, respectively.

articleTitle: Signaling and control in optical networks
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: Summary form only given. Core-network provisioning and restoration structures are currently under siege. With the floodgates of broadband access about to open wide, this siege is about to intensify. Despite recent enthusiasm for terabit routers as a means of addressing this need, it has become apparent that in fact a core circuit-switching layer that interconnect WDM systems with data-networking devices is, for economic and scaling reasons, the clear architecture of choice. However, traditional circuit-switching approaches lack the signaling and control features that are essential for delivering real-time network services. We discuss the rich emerging arsenal of techniques by which Internet protocol (IP)-centric signaling and control mechanisms, together with sophisticated routing algorithms, can be harnessed to supply the critical signaling and control features needed in evolving optical core networks.

articleTitle: Design of extended WDM access system for providing broadband communication and broadcast TV services
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We propose extended WDM access system employing optical packet/SCM hybrid amplification scheme for supporting larger number of subscribers. For suppressing interference between optical packets and SCM signal, optimum operating conditions of EDFA are discussed.

articleTitle: DWDM/SCM bi-directional interleaved transmission of 64-QAM using electro absorption modulated laser transmitters
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We demonstrate error free bi-directional interleaved DWDM/SCM transmission of 64-QAM over more than 200 km of fiber, using EML transmitters. Four-wave mixing and Rayleigh backscattering suppression are achieved in a dense bi-directional architecture.

articleTitle: High-performance photonic analog-to-digital converters
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: The advantages of photonics combined with advances in electronics has led to recent progress toward the realization of photonic analog-to-digital converters with wide-bandwidth and high-resolution. Applications, advantages, issues and recent results will be presented.

articleTitle: Nonlinear crosstalk suppression in a WDM analog fiber system by complementary modulation of twin carriers
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: By using complementary modulation of two closely-spaced optical carriers, nonlinear crosstalk on other carriers in WDM analog fiber communication systems can be greatly reduced. We have obtained up to 30 dB reduction at low modulation frequencies, where crosstalk is most severe.

articleTitle: Advanced return-path cable TV access technologies
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: The return-path dense wavelength-division-multiplexed network architecture using time -division-multiplexing and frequency-stacking methods is reviewed. Digitizing the return-path bandwidth provides significant cost savings while maintaining network transparency and flexibility.

articleTitle: Optical label swapping for IP-WDM networks using self-seeded Fabry-Perot laser label and fiber Bragg gratings
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We experimentally demonstrate a simple optical label swapping technique for 10 Gb/s IP-WDM networks using the self-seeded Fabry-Perot laser label and fiber Bragg gratings. Negligible power penalty of 0.1 - 0.2 dB can be achieved for both the 120-MHz label and the swapped label. In addition, tolerable power penalty of 0.6 dB for the data payload is obtained.

articleTitle: Polarimetric four-wave mixing between two wavelengths in a single-mode fiber
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We demonstrate experimentally a new polarimetric four-wave-mixing process in a single-mode fiber with two wavelengths. This process can result in polarization-induced crosstalk among WDM channels, yet has potential applications in wavelength conversion.

articleTitle: Comparison between different configurations of hybrid Raman/erbium-doped fiber amplifiers
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: A comprehensive theoretical study on the optimal configuration of hybrid fiber amplifiers is carried out yielding a closed form analysis. The maximum reachable distance is plotted against the span length and nonlinear weight, given a target OSNR.

articleTitle: 1 THz repetition rate multichannel pulse train source using an arrayed waveguide grating
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: 1 THz repetition rate bursts of short pulses at multiple spatially separated output channels are demonstrated from a single short pulse source laser and an arrayed waveguide grating designed to have a free spectral range less than the bandwidth of the source laser.

articleTitle: A sampled or superstructure grating tunable twin-guide laser for wide tunability with 2 tuning currents
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: A new widely tunable laser structure is proposed, a tunable twin guide (TTG) laser with 2 different sampled or superstructure gratings. This widely tunable laser only requires 2 instead of 3 tuning currents and has a much shorter cavity length than existing widely tunable laser diodes.

articleTitle: Experimental validation of an extended ABCD model for actively mode-locked fiber lasers
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: An extended ABCD model for actively mode-locked fiber lasers is presented. This new scheme includes the amplifier model taking into account the power evolution along the cavity fiber. The first experimental validation is reported.

articleTitle: 2 /spl times/ 2 wavelength-selective cross connect capable of switching 128 channels in sets of 8
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We present an efficient 2 /spl times/ 2 wavelength selective cross connect that is serviceable without interrupting traffic. It can handle over a hundred channels in a compact fashion by operating on them in sets. The 50-GHz-spaced passbands are flat topped with no gaps between them.

articleTitle: Expanded single mode fiber
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We present a solution to maintain an expanded mode in the extremity of a single mode fiber by using a piece-of multimode step index fiber. With a 25 /spl mu/m spot size, the average connection loss is 0.36 dB (without Fresnel reflection) for a multimode section length inferior to 5 cm. This process is particularly suitable for expanded beam connectors and fiber matrices.

articleTitle: Third- and fourth-order active dispersion compensation using a phase modulator in a terabit/s OTDM transmission
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: The third- and fourth-order dispersions of a transmission line were simultaneously compensated for by using a phase modulator. The pulse broadening of a 380 fs pulse after a 70 km transmission in a 1.28 Tbit/s OTDM experiment was as small as 20 fs.

articleTitle: All-optical serial-parallel data converters using optical interferometers
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We propose new simple and easily expandable schemes of all-optical serial-to-parallel and parallel-to-serial data converters based on optical interferometers. We experimentally demonstrate the proposed data converters.

articleTitle: Quality enhancement of a WDM signal using dispersion-imbalanced, loop mirror
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: The nonlinear filtering of a 10 Gb/s data stream in a dispersion-imbalanced fibre loop mirror has been demonstrated over a wide spectral range of 28 nm. A relative extinction ratio of 30 dB for the cw background has been achieved across the whole spectral range.

articleTitle: 40 Gb/s RZ unrepeatered transmission over 252 km SMF using Raman amplification
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We report on 40 Gb/s RZ-transmission over the record length of 252 km standard single-mode fiber using distributed Raman amplification. Effects of pulse width and dispersion compensation were investigated both, theoretically and experimentally.

articleTitle: Stability of the change of the third-order nonlinearity in silica fibre
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: The change of third order nonlinearity in silica fibre caused by poling is stable under UV or thermal erasure. The third order nonlinearity, like the linear refractive index, can be modulated by UV irradiation alone.

articleTitle: Wavelength-selectable microarray light sources simultaneously fabricated on a wafer covering the entire C-band
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We developed multi-range wavelength-selectable light sources (WSLs) with an all-selective MOVPE (ASM) grown microarray planar-buried-hetero (MPBH) structure. We simultaneously fabricated five WSLs, each with a unique 8-nm tuning range, to cover forty 100-GHz-spaced channels (the entire C-band). Uniform characteristics, such as an I/sub th/ of 8.3 /spl plusmn/ 1.2 mA, an SMSR of over 45 dB, and a fiber-coupled power up to 15 mW, were obtained.

articleTitle: Spiral fiber gratings for mode coupling
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We present some coupling properties of spiral fiber gratings. LP/sub 01/ modes in spiral fiber gratings were demonstrated and analyzed to couple efficiently to both LP/sub 11/ even and odd modes. LP/sub 01/ modes were shown to efficiently couple to both LP/sub 11/ even and odd modes by spiral gratings as predicted. A spiral fiber grating that converts the LP/sub 01/ mode equally to LP/sub 11/ even and odd modes, and a spiral grating that appreciably converts the LP/sub 01/ mode back to the same LP/sub 01/ mode through the LP/sub 01/-to-LP/sub 11/ and LP/sub 11/-to-LP/sub 01/ processes, were also demonstrated and analyzed.

articleTitle: Stability and jitter of an actively mode-locked dispersion-managed fiber ring laser
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We theoretically study the timing and energy jitter of an actively mode-locked dispersion-managed fiber ring laser. We show that the jitter is significantly dependent on the location of the filter, amplifier, and modulator in the cavity.

articleTitle: Simultaneous multi-channel PMD equalization for WDM systems
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: Summary form only given. We confirmed a simultaneous multi-channel PMD equalization scheme for WDM channels by simulation, which consists of a variable lattice optical circuit, WDM-DMUX, channel PMD monitors. The steepest-descent method shows successful multi-channel PMD equalization.

articleTitle: All-fiber passively Q-switched low-threshold erbium laser
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: A novel all-fiber passively Q-switched erbium laser with a Co/sup 2+/:ZnSe crystal as a saturable absorber is demonstrated experimentally and simulated numerically.

articleTitle: Design and fabrication of dispersion-managed fibers by periodic etching during the MCVD process
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We propose a new method of design and fabrication for a dispersion-managed fiber from a preform fabricated by a single MCVD process. Periodic etching during the MCVD process is used to change the index structure of the preform periodically along the longitudinal direction. A prototype fiber verifying the scheme has been fabricated.

articleTitle: Ultrafast laser pulse spectral domain differential phase shift keying
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: Pulse spectral-domain differential-phase-shift-keying has been demonstrated using AOM-based pulse shaping for modulation and spectral interferometry for demodulation. The encoded differential phase is successfully retrieved despite of the nonlinear distortions after 4-km dispersion-shifted fiber transmission.

articleTitle: Wavelength-tunable soliton generation in the 1400 -1600 nm region using an Yb fiber laser
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: Soliton pulses tunable in the 1400 - 1600 nm region are generated in standard telecom fiber seeded with a continuum produced in a fiber taper using an Yb fiber laser. Here we demonstrate supercontinuum generation in the 500 nm - 1600 nm wavelength region using a compact ultrafast Yb fiber laser as a systems-compatible pump source for the first time. Moreover, by injecting the supercontinuum into a length of standard telecommunications fiber, we can induce Raman-soliton generation to produce near bandwidth-limited pulses tunable in the 1400 - 1600 nm wavelength region. The required pulse energy for supercontinuum and Raman-soliton generation is only of the order of 1 nJ, which demonstrates that this technique is compatible with fiber sources operating at GHz repetition rates.

articleTitle: Pulse width dependence of polarization mode dispersion and polarization dependent loss for a pulse and their impacts on pulse broadening
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: The interaction of polarization mode dispersion and polarization dependent loss for an optical pulse is studied. The pulse-width-dependence of polarization mode dispersion and dependent loss, and their combined effect on pulse broadening will be discussed.

articleTitle: GHz bandwidth-efficiency resonant cavity enhanced ITO-Schottky photodiodes
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We demonstrated high-performance resonant cavity enhanced ITO-Schottky photodiodes. We achieved a peak efficiency of 75% around 820 nm with a 3-dB bandwidth of 60 GHz resulting in a bandwidth-efficiency product of 45 GHz.

articleTitle: Tunable wavelength filter with a single-mode grating fiber thinned by plasma etching
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We studied a tunable wavelength filter using a single-mode Bragg grating fiber with a cladding thinned by reactive plasma etching. The reflection wavelength shifts were demonstrated by controlling the effective refractive index or the period of the grating.

articleTitle: Update on optical component reliability and testing requirements
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: Optical component reliability, as underway in international standards, is reviewed. In optical communications, the reliability functions of fiber and optoelectronic semiconductor transceivers, has been extensively studied and modeled for some time. The mechanisms causing failure for these are relatively well known. The mechanisms in other items such as passive optical components, optical amplifiers, or dynamic components (that are optically passive but electrically active) are not nearly as well understood.

articleTitle: Simple and robust 40 GHz RZ pulse source based on a fiber optical parametric amplifier
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We demonstrate a simple 40 GHz RZ source based on a fiber optical parametric amplifier. By using a narrowband 40 GHz sinusoidally intensity modulated pump, stable, nearly chirp free, high power, 2-4 ps wide pulses are obtained over 37 nm, extended into the L-band.

articleTitle: Construction of a single/multiple wavelength RZ optical pulse source at 40 GHz by use of wavelength conversion in a high-nonlinearity DSF-NOLM
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: A single or multiple wavelength RZ optical pulse source at 40 GHz is successfully obtained by using wavelength conversion in a nonlinear optical loop mirror consisting of high nonlinearity-dispersion shifted fiber.

articleTitle: Fiber dependence and coupling efficiency limitation for a lensed fiber integrated with a long period fiber grating
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We analyze the fiber dependence and the efficiency limitation for optical coupling using a lensed fiber integrated with a long period fiber grating. In summary, the fiber dependence and the efficiency limitation is analyzed for optical coupling using a lensed fiber integrated with a long-period fiber grating (LPFG). We found that a dispersion-shifted fiber is more efficient for the proposed coupling scheme than a standard single-mode fiber. The coupling efficiency seems to be strongly reduced for a small beam waist owing to the effects of fiber truncation and spherical aberration. A high coupling efficiency may be obtained for the LD-to-fiber coupling scheme if a hyperbolic lensed fiber is used.

articleTitle: Statistical analyses of PMD using Monte Carlo method for different configuration of loose tube optical cable
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: Presents a statistical analysis of PMD for different configuration of loose tube optical cable. We have shown that it is possible to specify a PMD statistical upper limit based on the optical cable project.

articleTitle: Adiabatic coupling in tapered air-silica microstructured optical fiber
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We study adiabatic mode propagation in tapered air-silica microstructured optical fibers and demonstrate efficient coupling into a robust high-delta microstructured optical fiber. As an application of this device, we exploit the widely flattened dispersion and enhanced peak intensity in the waist of the tapered microstructured fiber to generate tunable self-frequency shifting. Raman solitons over the communications window from 1.3 /spl mu/m to 1.65 /spl mu/m.

articleTitle: Cladding mode effect in superstructure fiber Bragg gratings and its applications in simultaneous strain and temperature measurement
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: Periodically modulated exposure makes the superstructure fiber Bragg grating functions as a long-period grating and so introduce broad-band loss peaks in the transmission spectrum. This characteristic has applications in simultaneous measurement for temperature and strain.

articleTitle: Polarization mode dispersion in optical communication systems
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: Summary form only given. Polarisation mode dispersion (PMD) is a major impairment for high-bit-rate optical systems. The objective of this course is threefold: (1) understand the physical phenomena of PMD, (2) review the current status of understanding of the impact of PMD on optical systems, and (3) PMD mitigation approaches. In this course we will introduce the concept of PMD and its various mathematical description briefly with emphasis on visualizing and comparing different ways of describing PMD. Then, very briefly, we will concentrate on some measurement aspects of PMD in systems. Current understanding of PMD impact on systems will be summarized next. System impact of PMD will be reviewed in three stages. (1) Impact of fiber PMD, 1st and higher order, in high-bit-rate systems in presence of chromatic dispersion. (2) Impact of fiber and discrete component PMD on optical systems. (3) Impact of fiber and component PMD on optical systems in presence of polarization dependent loss. Finally, PMD mitigation approaches will be discussed.

articleTitle: System impact of phase ripples in optical components
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We show that facet reflections in optical components induce a sine-shaped chromatic dispersion ripple. We furthermore investigate the system impact of it. We conclude that the maximum value of chromatic dispersion is not a relevant parameter as long as the frequency scale of variation of the chromatic dispersion is below the spectral bandwidth of the signal.

articleTitle: A high-power, low-noise polarization maintaining Erbium/Brillouin fiber amplified source
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: A polarization maintaining erbium/Brillouin fiber amplifier was investigated. The output noise of the amplified source was measured and compared to shot-noise. Shot-noise limited performance was achieved within the 1 GHz to 8 GHz frequency band.

articleTitle: Performance prediction method for distributed Raman amplification in installed fiber systems based on OTDR data
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: Novel characterization method of the loss profiles in transmission paths for distributed Raman amplification is proposed, which accurately predicts the gain and noise figure from conventional optical time domain reflectometry data.

articleTitle: Multiwavelength fiber lasers with tunable wavelength spacing
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We propose and demonstrate multiwavelength fiber lasers with tunable wavelength spacing. A tunable spacing filter consists of polarizers and a PMF. By changing the stress position on the PMF, the spacing can be controlled.

articleTitle: Optimum span configuration of Raman-amplifier dispersion-managed fibers
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We analyze the influence of the span structure on the performance of Raman-amplified dispersion-managed fibers. Our calculations show that a configuration with the dispersion compensating fiber placed in the span center achieves the best trade-off between optical signal-to-noise ratio and nonlinear effects.

articleTitle: The dispersion-free filters for DWDM systems using 30 mm long symmetric fiber Bragg gratings
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: The dispersion-free FBG is designed by applying the optimized cosine-progression to the apodization profile. As experimental results show that it offers the suitable filter, with 25 dB crosstalk, 15 ps group delay, for high bit-rate DWDM systems.

articleTitle: A novel 240-Gbps channel-by-channel dedicated optical protection ring network using wavelength selective switches
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: A novel optical add-drop multiplex (OADM) node architecture design using wavelength selective switches is proposed. We demonstrate experimentally the OADM configuration and optical channel dedicated protection in a two-fiber ring network with 24/spl times/10-Gbps DWDM traffic.

articleTitle: Accurate calculation of eye diagrams and error rates in long-haul transmission systems
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We found the distribution of phase and timing jitter in a DMS system to be Gaussian-distributed. After their removal, the residual noise Fourier components obey a multivariate-Gaussian distribution, allowing us to accurately calculate eye diagrams and error rates.

articleTitle: 43-Gbit/s OTN interface prototype
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: Reports, for the first time, a 43-Gbit/s OTN interface prototype that implements more system functions than optical sending/reception, such as framing, scrambling/de-scrambling, client mapping, and supervisory functions, all with high performance.

articleTitle: Study on the pumping wavelength dependency of S/sup +/-band fluoride based thulium doped fiber amplifiers
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We present the pump wavelength dependency of a S/sup +/-band thulium doped fluoride fiber amplifier by using a newly developed numerical model for the 1.47 /spl mu/m amplification band. This is for the first time to authors' knowledge. The optimum pump wavelength varies from 1045 nm to 1070 nm depending on the operating conditions. Insights on the amplifier operation dependence on the pump wavelength and pumping power will be discussed.

articleTitle: Analysis of the dispersion properties of holey optical fibers using normalized dispersion
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: The dispersion property of holey optical fibers with the complicated refractive index structure is investigated using the numerical Galerkin's method. A new useful concept of the normalized dispersion are introduced.

articleTitle: WDM optical packet transmission experiment over 235 km of installed fibers
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: 100-GHz spaced 16-channel WDM optical packets generated by a super-structure-grating (SSG)-DBR laser were transmitted over 235 km of installed DSFs at the line rate of 2.48832 Gb/s and packet length of 2 kbytes.

articleTitle: Limitations of 40 Gbit/s based dispersion managed WDM transmission: solitons versus quasi-linear propagation regime
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We investigate the transmission performance covering the whole spectrum of dispersion managed propagation regimes ranging from soliton to quasi-linear RZ propagation, detailing the limiting factors and optimal performance conditions.

articleTitle: FEC techniques in submarine transmission systems
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: Describes different concatenated coding schemes for submarine transmission system. Simulation results demonstrate a net coding gain of about 8 dB for hard decoding strategy and up to 10 dB when using iterative soft decoding. The impact of the FEC net coding gain margin in a transoceanic submarine system is discussed.

articleTitle: Silica GIO fibers with high performance
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: A silica graded-index oval-core (GIO) fiber that can transform an elliptical field with an aspect ratio of 3.8 to a circular one, and vice versa, has been fabricated for the first time. The fiber promises low-loss coupling between high-power pumping LDs and single-mode fibers.

articleTitle: Analysis on the limitation of PMD compensator in the 10 Gbps transmission system with polarization dependent loss
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We analyze the effects of polarisation dependent loss (PDL) in the highspeed transmission system, under the polarisation mode dispersion (PMD) compensation environment. As the link PDL increases, the BER enhancement from the PMD compensator decreases sharply, making the PMD compensation technique much ineffective. Analysis with an 80 km, 10 Gbps system shows that even a minute link PDL of 0.5 dB could seriously limit the system performance.

articleTitle: Modeling short optical pulse generation using electroabsorption modulators
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: Model short optical pulse generation in sinusoidally-driven lumped-electrode electroabsorption modulators, describes pulse width scaling with device and applied modulation parameters, and defines a new device figure of merit.

articleTitle: High performance, 64-chip, 160 Gchip/s fiber grating based OCDMA receiver incorporating a nonlinear optical loop mirror
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We demonstrate a grating based 64-chip, 160 Gchip/s optical code division multiple access (OCDMA) system incorporating a nonlinear optical loop mirror (NOLM) within the receiver to enhance the code recognition signature. Error-free, penalty-free operation is obtained with complete recovery of the original input pulse shape in a range of transmission experiments.

articleTitle: Millimetre-wave over fibre transmission using a BPSK reference-modulated optical injection phase-lock loop
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We report generation of single sideband millimetre-wave modulated optical signals by a reference-modulated optical injection phase-lock loop. A 36 GHz 68 Mbit/s BPSK signal is transmitted over 25 km of unamplified SMF with 8 dB optical power margin and BER<10/sup -9/.

articleTitle: Fully monolithically integrated 40-Gbit/s transmitter and receiver
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: 40-Gbit/s ETDM transmitter and receiver, both with a 10-Gbit/s interface have been developed. All ICs used in the transmitter and receiver are integrated monolithically by using InP HBTs and SiGe HBTs.

articleTitle: S-band all-Raman amplifiers for 40 /spl times/ 10 Gb/s transmission over 6 /spl times/ 100 km of non-zero dispersion fiber
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We present S-band Raman amplifiers that compensate both dispersion and span loss using distributed and discrete amplification over 1488/1518 nm. We transmitted 40 /spl times/ 10 Gb/s over 6 /spl times/ 100 km of a prototype TrueWave/sup AE/ fiber.

articleTitle: 2.56 Tb/s capacity, 0.8 b/Hz.s DWDM transmission over 120 km NDSF using polarisation-bit-interleaved 80 Gb/s OTDM signal
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We report on the generation and transmission of a polarisation-bit-interleaved 80 Gb/s signal at 0.8 b/Hz.s spectral efficiency. A total capacity of 2.56 Tb/s (32/spl times/80 Gb/s) was demonstrated over 120 km NDSF with distributed Raman amplification. System linear Q values between 6.1 and 8 for 2/sup 31/-1 PRBS pattern length were achieved.

articleTitle: Chirped duobinary transmission (CDBT) for mitigating the self-phase modulation limiting effect
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We present a new modulation format called chirped duobinary transmission (CDBT). The dispersion limited transmission distance of conventional chirp-free duobinary transmission is enlarged significantly, especially in the nonlinear regime by interaction of SPM and chirp.

articleTitle: Penalties through XPM crosstalk in a switched long haul standard fiber WDM system based on normalized transmission sections
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: For the first time penalties due to XPM crosstalk have been measured by switching neighbouring channels in a long distance 16/spl times/10 Gb/s ASK NRZ system based on standard single mode fibre (SMF) links with dispersion optimized transmission sections.

articleTitle: Finite-band noise theory and experiment for four-wave mixing in RZ transmission systems
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: The finite-band noise theory of four wave mixing (FWM) is introduced. It was validated using simulations and experiments. It predicts FWM noise scaling with bit alignment among channels and enables comparisons between RZ and NRZ modulation formats. We introduced a general finite-band technique for calculating the contribution of FWM to Q and validated it using both numerical simulations and laboratory experiments. This theory shows that the level of FWM noise or cross talk decreases as the bit slots are shifted and that the FWM Q for RZ formatted data tends to be larger than that in systems with NRZ modulation.

articleTitle: 40 Gb/s tandem electro-absorption modulator
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: NRZ and RZ data transmission at 40 Gb/s are demonstrated for the first time using buried heterostructure tandem electro-absorption modulators monolithically integrated with a semiconductor optical amplifier and input/output spot-size converters. Zero penalty RZ transmission over a 100 km dispersion managed link is achieved.

articleTitle: An efficient electrically tunable all-fiber polarization controller
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We demonstrate a novel electrically tunable all-fiber polarization controller using evaporated micro-heaters on short sections of polarization maintaining fiber. Potential applications include compact, low loss, economical polarization controllers for characterization of PDL (polarization dependent loss) or PMD (polarization mode dispersion) compensation.

articleTitle: S-band amplifier with variable gain tilt control
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We present a method of variable gain tilt control for a thulium doped fiber amplifier (TDFA) using a mid-stage attenuator, together with measurements of the amplifier performance. The addition of tilt control allows S-band amplifiers to be used with a wide array of fibers and channel configurations since the effect of both Raman interactions and the O-H absorption peak can be compensated at installation. This is particularly important when adding amplifiers to an existing system, which may not be fully characterized in the S and S+ bands. The simplicity of using a variable attenuator to produce gain tilt, combined with the very short active-fiber lengths, allows manufacture at similar costs to erbium amplifiers.

articleTitle: 1400 - 1480 nm ridge-waveguide pump lasers with 1 watt CW output power for EDFA and Raman amplification
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: High power ridge-waveguide (RWG) lasers with emission wavelengths from 1400 to 1480 nm have been developed to meet the demands of high channel density EDFA and Raman amplification systems. Output power levels as high as 1 watt from the RWG device can be effectively coupled to single-mode optical fiber producing ex-fiber powers as high as 710 mW.

articleTitle: All-fiber wavelength-tunable acousto-optic switch
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We describe a novel all-fiber wavelength-tunable acousto-optic switch utilizing intermodal coupling in a two-mode fiber. Low loss (/spl sim/2 dB) operation was possible due to its all-fiber configuration with a fiber acousto-optic tunable filter and a mode-selective coupler.

articleTitle: Error free 2.5 Gb/s transmission over 125 km conventional fiber of a directly modulated widely tunable vertical cavity surface emitting laser
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: A vertical cavity surface emitting laser with over 35 nm tuning range is modulated through its optical pumping at rates up to 2.5 Gb/s. Error free transmission is obtained for a conventional fiber of 125 km.

articleTitle: Value proposition for configurable optical network elements
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: The value of configurable optical network elements for the fast provisioning of wavelength services is assessed against manual provisioning. Results are presented that were obtained by evaluating the long haul wavelength circuit provisioning process.

articleTitle: Highly efficient 980 nm single mode modules with over 0.5 Watt pump power
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We present narrow beam divergence InGaAs/AlGaAs 980 nm ridge waveguide laser diodes with over 1 W CW-rollover power. Together with superior power conversion efficiency a maximum fiber-coupled light output power of over 0.5 W has been reached.

articleTitle: 1 Tbit/s (101/spl times/10 Gbit/s) transmission over transpacific distance using 28 nm C-band EDFAs
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We present the first Tbit/s transpacific (9000 km) transmission experiment over the EDFA C-band. Using 101 channels at 10 Gbit/s spaced 33 GHz apart, a slope-matched dispersion map and an advanced gain equalization technique, we demonstrate a system margin of 4 dB above the forward error correction (FEC) limit.

articleTitle: High gain short length phosphate glass erbium-doped fiber amplifier material
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: An internal gain of 10 dB (975 nm pumping) has been demonstrated from a 2.2 cm long section of experimental fiber manufactured from Kigre's "MM-2" Er,Yb:phosphate laser glass. As much as 26 dB (1480 nm pumping) of gain Was produced from this same experimental fiber with an 8.8 cm length. Images of the 1.54 /spl mu/m mode field containment for this fiber indicate a perfect match to standard communications transmission fiber.

articleTitle: Four wave mixing induced changes in the noise spectrum in an optical fiber
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: Structures are observed in the noise spectrum propagated in dispersion-shifted fibers in the presence of two lasers. Four wave mixing (FWM) interactions provide gain or increased loss at particular wavelengths which permits identification of. the various fiber zero-dispersion wavelengths.

articleTitle: Statistical measurement of the combined effect of PMD and PDL using a 10-Gb/s recirculating loop testbed
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: The combined effect of polarisation mode dispersion (PMD) and polarization dependent loss (PDL) is investigated statistically using a 10-Gb/s, 8/spl times/82-km, recirculating fiber-loop testbed. As average PDL varies from 1.0 to 2.1 dB with a fixed average PMD of 18 ps, the power penalty at 2% probability increases from 2.5 to 4.3 dB.

articleTitle: Ultrafast wavelength and polarization insensitive all-optical clock recovery
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: Wavelength and polarization insensitive all-optical clock recovery based on a two-section gain-coupled DFB laser and cross gain conversion has been demonstrated. The lockup time of clock recovery is less than 1 ns.

articleTitle: Bi-directional WDM transmission by use of SOAs as inline amplifiers without isolators
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: Error-free bi-directional transmission of 8/spl times/10 Gb/s signals over two inline SOAs is realized for the first time. It is demonstrated that SOAs can be used for inline amplifiers in bidirectional multi-wavelength transmission systems at 10 Gb/s without any isolator.

articleTitle: 2/spl times/40-channel dispersion-slope compensator for 40-Gbit/s WDM transmission systems covering entire C- and L-bands
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We demonstrate a 2/spl times/40-channel dispersion-slope compensator that employed an arrayed-waveguide grating (AWG) and a spatial filter. It can compensate for the dispersion slope of the entire bandwidth of C- and L-bands simultaneously.

articleTitle: Polarization multiplexed 2/spl times/20 Gbit/s RZ transmission using interference detection
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: Polarization division multiplex doubles optical fiber capacity. Interchannel interference is detected in the RX and employed as a control signal for polarization tracking. Transmission over 33 km of DSF with a 6.25 ps polarisation mode dispersion (PMD) tolerance is demonstrated.

articleTitle: Novel technique for measuring the residual stress and the photoelastic effect profile of an optical fiber
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: A novel method is demonstrated for determining the photoelastic effect profile as well as the residual stress profile of an optical fiber for the first time. Measurement results of the residual stress profiles and the photoelastic effect profiles of a B-Ge doped fiber and an Er-Al doped fiber are demonstrated by using this technique with its spatial resolution better than 0.8 pm.

articleTitle: Estimation of polarization dispersion parameters for compensation with reduced feedback
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: A scheme for polarization dispersion compensation with reduced feedback is explored. Repeatable estimates of the PMD vector have been obtained from polarimeter measurements using various algorithms. Limitations due to higher-order PMD are discussed.

articleTitle: High power gain-clamped EDFAs with flat gain
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: A two-stage all optical gain-clamped EDFA is designed for high output power to handle 64 channel WDM network systems. The EDFA has gain-clamped output powers up to 22 dBm with a flat gain bandwidth over 30 nm.

articleTitle: Sideband instability in the presence of periodic power variation and periodic dispersion management
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: The analytical expression of sideband instability effect considering both periodic power variation and periodic dispersion management is derived. The result shows that the magnitude of sideband instability (SI) gain varies with the change of strength of dispersion management.

articleTitle: Bi-directional optical microwave transmission using a base station without DC electric power supply
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: Bi-directional optical microwave transmission was performed using a base station composed of a bias free electric absorption modulator and a uni-traveling carrier photodiode. Error free operation was performed for down- and up-stream data links.

articleTitle: Multi-fiber-chip-coupling modules for monolithically integrated Mach-Zehnder interferometers for TDM/WDM communication systems
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We designed and fabricated multi-fiber modules for arrayed waveguide-fed InP-OEICs like monolithically integrated MZIs. The light output is collected with high efficiency into tapered SMF arrays which are fixed by gluing in a special designed set-up.

articleTitle: Dispersion mitigation using a fiber-Bragg-grating sideband filter and a tunable electronic equalizer
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: Error-free transmission (PRBS 2/sup 23/-1, BER=10/sup -9/) over 225 km non-dispersion shifted standard singlemode fiber is demonstrated at 10 Gbit/s using a vestigial sideband signal generated with a fiber Bragg grating. Electrical dispersion equalization is assisted by a transversal filter SiGe chip.

articleTitle: Optical backbone topology design under traffic aggregation and flexibility constraints
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We present an analysis and propose a heuristic-based approach for the major issue of localization of traffic aggregation points for optical networks. The method is applied on a US topology showing granularity and by-pass effects. Our purpose here is to build an optimized integrated architecture taking into account potential redundancy of resource in the networks and the jumps of capacity and granularity between optical and electronic domains. Although, we demonstrate that squeezing the most out of WDM introduction requires a well defined strategy for the optical backbone design.

articleTitle: Bidirectional optical code division multiplexed field trial system for the metro and access area
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: A fully operational bidirectional optical code division multiplexed system has been successfully implemented within the KomNet field trial. 4/spl times/155.52 Mbit/s signals each in up- and downlink are transmitted over a 20 km two fibre feeder. Transmission of the signals over DWDM metro rings is discussed.

articleTitle: Detailed experimental characterization of the chirp properties of an SOA-MZI wavelength converter
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: The chirp properties for an SOA-MZI wavelength converter are characterized based on measurements of the /spl alpha/-parameter. Results for three optical modulators with quite different chirp properties demonstrate that the chirp of the converted signal is essentially independent of the chirp of the input signal.

articleTitle: Enhanced PSBT: demonstration of dispersion tolerance and noise resistance over 300 km terrestrial link
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We study the dispersion management of enhanced phase-shaped binary transmission (EPSBT) at 10 Gb/s over a typical 300 km-long terrestrial link of SMF, varying the pre- and post-compensating DCF fiber. We compare the chromatic dispersion maps for span powers of 1 dBm and 6 dBm, where nonlinear effects influence the propagation, and show that the tolerance characteristics of EPSBT are maintained even at a span power of +6 dBm, typical for field applications.

articleTitle: An efficient wavelength assignment algorithm for service and restoration in WDM rings
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We present a vertex-coloring based service and restoration wavelength assignment algorithm for WDM rings. Through performance bounds and simulations, we show that this algorithm achieves low wavelength requirement, and is suitable for reducing fault-monitoring costs.

articleTitle: Error-free 100/spl times/10 Gbit/s unrepeatered transmission over 350 km
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: Error-free unrepeatered transmission of 100 channels at 10 Gbit/s is demonstrated over 350 km. Enabling technologies are remote amplification, dual wavelength Raman preamplification and forward error correction leading to the longest error-free 1 Tbit/s unrepeatered transmission.

articleTitle: Fusion spliceable and highly efficient Bi/sub 2/O/sub 3/-based EDF for short-length and broadband application pumped at 1480 nm
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: A conventional fusion splicing to SiO/sub 2/ fiber was achieved in W/sub 2/O/sub 3/-based Er doped fibers (EDF). High slope efficiency of 43 % and broadband gain spectrum were achieved at 1490 nm pumping amplification for only 26 cm-length.

articleTitle: Low insertion-loss and high isolation polymeric Y-branching thermo-optic switch with partitioned heater
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: A thermo-optic switch with low insertion-loss and high isolation was realized using a polymeric Y-branching waveguide. The partitioned heater greatly improves the isolation. Over 40dB isolation was achieved with the low insertion loss of 1.8dB.

articleTitle: Inline loopbacks for improved OSNR and reduced double Rayleigh scattering in distributed Raman amplifiers
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We present a novel transmission system configuration, using passive components in a loopback topology, to improve counter-pumped distributed Raman amplification. This improves system performance, reduces double Rayleigh scattering and increases the efficiency of pump usage.

articleTitle: TDM/SCM label encoding and extraction technique for lightpath control and trail monitoring
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We have proposed and demonstrated a novel label encoding and extraction technique on optical channels using direct TDM/SCM generation from data bit-streams. This technique allows lightpath-control and trail-monitoring maintaining transparency on all optical transport elements.

articleTitle: Efficient tunable fiber ring laser for 1580 nm band with a fiber Bragg grating
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: An efficient tunable erbium-doped fiber ring laser for 1580 nm band is realized by injecting conventional band amplified spontaneous emission with a fiber Bragg grating. The insertion of the fiber Bragg grating reduces the lasing threshold by a half. The tuning range is from 1560 to 1610 nm with signal to noise ratio better than 60 dB.

articleTitle: A 4-channel WDM/OCDMA system incorporating 255-chip, 320 Gchip/s quaternary phase coding and decoding gratings
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We report four channel WDM/OCDMA experiments using superstructured fiber Bragg gratings for coding and decoding. The codes are four times longer (255 chips) and have twice the chip rate (320 Gchip/s) of any previously reported direct sequence OCDMA demonstration. As far as we are aware, this is also the first experimental demonstration of quaternary phase coding in OCDMA.

articleTitle: Single to multi wavelength conversion using amplified spontaneous emission of semiconductor optical amplifier
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: A wavelength conversion technique which can convert an input signal to many wavelengths simultaneously without any probe laser is proposed. 622 Mb/s one-to-six wavelength conversion and multicast in a bus network are demonstrated.

articleTitle: Comparison of optical PMD compensation using variable and fixed differential group delays
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: Polarization mode dispersion compensation with dynamic tracking is investigated by modeling. An optical compensator using a variable differential group delay can alleviate the local minimum problem and provide superior performance compared to a fixed-delay compensator.

articleTitle: External-cavity tunable diode lasers for network deployment
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We report tunable lasers with exceptional performance: high output power, wide tuning range, precise wavelength control, high side-mode suppression ratio, and narrow linewidth all at the same time. These external cavity diode lasers are developed specifically for network deployment.

articleTitle: Investigation of single mode fiber coupling using diffractive optical element with continuous relief fabricated by focused ion beam technology
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: The design, microfabrication and testing of diffractive optical elements (DOE's) with continuous relief and their use in fiber coupling, is discussed in detail. DOE's with diameter as small as 65 /spl mu/m are realized by means of focused ion beam (FIB) technology. A focused Ga/sup +/ ion beam is used to mill a continuous relief microstructure at an acceleration voltage of 50 kV. From the results of the test, a coupling efficiency of 75% was achieved. This indicates that the DOE's were suitably designed within the application requirements and satisfactorily manufactured by using FIB.

articleTitle: High power InGaAsP/InP broad-waveguide single-mode ridge-waveguide lasers
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: Single-mode broad-waveguide separate confinement ridge-waveguide InGaAsP/InP diode lasers emitting in 1500 nm wavelength range have realized cw output power levels in excess of 400 mW. The high-power broad-waveguide structure design and ridge-waveguide fabrication technology along with device operational performance parameters will be discussed.

articleTitle: Benefit of Raman amplification in ultra-long-distance 40 Gbit/s-based WDM transmission
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: An optimum configuration for hybrid Raman/EDFA amplification in ultra-long-distance 40 Gbit/s WDM transmission was investigated. By optimizing the Raman gain, 16 /spl times/ 40 Gbit/s WDM transmission over 2000 km was achieved with 80 km amplifier spacing.

articleTitle: Fully functional optical add & drop multiplexer using twin-core fiber based Mach-Zehnder interferometer with photoimprinted fiber Bragg gratings
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: For the first time, a twin-core fiber based add and drop multiplexer, can both insert and extract the same wavelength with more than 30 dB adjacent crosstalk, rejection, and cross-state versus b ar-state isolation.

articleTitle: 96/spl times/11.4 Gbit/s transmission over 3,800 km using C-band EDFA and non-zero dispersion shifted fiber
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We have performed 96/spl times/11.4Gbit/s transmission over 3,800 km successfully using C-band EDFA and non-zero dispersion shifted fiber. The measured minimum Q of 96 channels is 15.1 dB, which gives sufficient margin for submarine cable systems.

articleTitle: Modeling and simulations for 10 Gb multimode optical fiber link component specifications
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We present simulations of a next-generation 10Gb multimode fiber link including effects of transmitters, fibers, and connections. The results support transmitter and fiber specifications proposed in the TIA FO2.2.1 working group.

articleTitle: Novel S-band amplification and wavelength conversion technique using dual nonlinear phenomena
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We demonstrate a new S-band nonlinear fibre amplifier, with over 18 dB gain, and S-band wavelength converter, with over 20 nm bandwidth, obtained by combination of Raman gain and optical parametric amplification.

articleTitle: Baseband optical carrier-sense multiple access - demonstration and sensitivity measurements
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We demonstrate for the first time baseband optical carrier-sense multiple access with collision avoidance. We evaluate the performance of the baseband carrier-sense circuit with bit- and packet-error-rate measurements. The sensitivity of the carrier-sense circuit is -51.6 dBm.

articleTitle: Regenerated 40 Gbit/s long-haul transmission using all-optical SOA-MZI as loss-free synchronous modulator
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We propose a novel regenerator scheme using a 40 Gbit/s SOA-based Mach-Zehnder interferometer (SOA-MZI) for performing optical regeneration by synchronous modulation. Experimental loop implementation of such a loss-free all-optical regenerator made it possible to demonstrate an error-free 40 Gbit/s transmission over 10,000 km with 2/sup 23/-1 PRBS sequence.

articleTitle: Resonant intra-channel four-wave mixing in strongly dispersion-managed transmission systems
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: Intra-channel four-wave mixing in a transmission system with strong periodic dispersion management is studied. The "ghost" pulse at the zero bit is shown to grow resonantly as a result of periodic forcing and temporal phase matching with the signal pulses.

articleTitle: Crosstalk in an eight-wavelength WDM analog lightwave system: measurement and analysis
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: The analysis of crosstalk in a two-wavelength system is extended to predict the crosstalk for an eight-wavelength channel system. It is found that RF power addition of the crosstalk from different channels provides the most reliable prediction of the measured crosstalk.

articleTitle: Universal conditions for nonlinear refractive index n/sub 2/ estimation of dispersion compensating fibers by CW-SPM method
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: Universal conditions for nonlinear refractive index n/sub 2/ estimation of dispersion compensating fibers by continuous wave (CW)-SPM method are investigated theoretically and experimentally. It is clarified that the required fiber length and the minimum power for n/sub 2/ estimation can be expressed as simple functions in terms of chromatic dispersion D. Moreover, it is experimentally confirmed that the present conditions for n/sub 2/ estimation are reasonable and that the n/sub 2/ value of DCF longer than the required fiber length is underestimated.

articleTitle: Broadband fiber optic amplifiers
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: Broadband fiber optic amplifiers are key elements of DWDM systems and enablers for optical networks. New amplifier technologies for extending gain-bandwidth and equalizing the power deviation among WDM signals are discussed toward the next generation of ultra.-high-capacity DWDM systems.

articleTitle: Metamorphic double heterojunction InGaAs-InGaAlAs-InAlAs photodiodes on GaAs substrates for 40 Gbit/s long wavelength optical fiber communication
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: Metamorphic InGaAs-InGaAlAs-InAlAs double heterojunction P-i-I-N photodiodes were fabricated on GaAs substrates and characterized. They exhibited a low dark current of 500 pA at 5 V bias, a responsivity of 0.6 A/W, and a n3 dB bandwidth of 38 GHz for 1.55 /spl mu/m light.

articleTitle: Low cross-talk 4ch PD array module assembled in plastic package for signal monitoring in DWDM system
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: A low cross-talk 4ch PD array module using the unique alignment method for signal monitoring in a DWDM system was developed. We analyzed the cross-talk mechanism and developed a new device structure for reducing it to as low as -40 dB.

articleTitle: Estimation of the SRS crosstalk on pilot-tones in WDM systems using a dither transfer matrix
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: The effect of stimulated Raman scattering (SRS) on pilot-tones and optical performance monitoring in a WDM system is considered by small signal analysis of the SRS equation and introducing a new concept-a dither transfer matrix (DTM).

articleTitle: New dispersion compensating module for compensation of dispersion and dispersion slope of non-zero dispersion fibres in the C-band
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: A new single mode dispersion compensating module with very low insertion loss and PMD for C-band compensation of TrueWave-RS/sup TM/ (TWRS/sup TM/) is presented. We show experimentally that the C-band link residual dispersion varies only 0.04 ps/(nm/spl middot/km).

articleTitle: Optimised 2R all-optical regenerator with low polarisation sensitivity penalty (<1 dB) for optical networking applications
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: 2R experiments at 10 Gbit/s have been performed using a low polarisation sensitivity SOA-Mach-Zehnder interferometer. Excess penalty below 1 dB due to polarisation sensitivity has been measured over 15 and 25 nm input wavelength range with respectively 21 and 25 dB/0.1 nm input OSNR.

articleTitle: Duobinary carrier-suppressed return-to-zero format and its application to 100 GHz-spaced 8/spl times/43-Gbit/s DWDM unrepeatered transmission over 163 km
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We propose the duobinary carrier-suppressed return-to-zero format; its bandwidth is less than 100 GHz at 43 Gbit/s. 100 GHz-spaced DWDM unrepeatered transmission is demonstrated over 163 km at +10 dBm/channel with the crosstalk penalty less than 1 dB.

articleTitle: Probability densities of depolarization associated with second-order PMD in optical fibers
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: The second-order polarisation mode dispersion (PMD) components associated with depolarization of the principal states can cause significant systems impairments.
