We describe the probability densities of these components and find excellent agreement between extensive measurements, simulations and theoretical predictions.

articleTitle: Low-cost, polarization insensitive photodiodes integrating spot size converters for 40 Gbits/s applications
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: High-speed photodiodes are realized with low-cost technology including etched waveguide input facet, antireflection coating on wafer and cleaving V-grooves. 0.46A/W responsivity, 40 GHz bandwidth, 6 mA saturation current, are simultaneously achieved with less than /spl plusmn/0.1 dB polarization dependence.

articleTitle: Comparison of erbium amplifier measurement using a high power amplified spontaneous emission source or using an ITU grid
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: An inexpensive ASE source, used for erbium, amplifier measurements, compares well with an ITU grid. Deltas between methods are less than 0.4 and 0.3 dB for gain and noise figure respectively. Spectral resolution is improved.

articleTitle: Large photosensitivity in germanosilicate planar waveguides induced by 157-nm F/sub 2/-laser radiation
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: The photosensitivity response of germanium-doped planar silica waveguides was characterized with 157-nm F/sub 2/ laser radiation. A small penetration depth of several microns provided refractive index changes above 10/sup -3/ with /spl sim/10-kJ/cm/sup 2/ total fluence.

articleTitle: Suppression of nonlinear effects in tellurite-based EDFAs by fiber parameter modification
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: Large nonlinear effects generated in L-band tellurite-based EDFAs can be suppressed to almost same extent as those generated in typical L-band silica-based EDFAs by increasing mode field diameter or shortening the EDF while increasing the Er/sup 3+/ concentration.

articleTitle: Micromachined curling optical switch array for PLC-based, integrated programmable add/drop multiplexer
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We propose a micromachined optical switch array which is suitable for integration in planar lightwave circuit. A programmable add/drop multiplexer fabricated using the micromechanical processing and silica techniques demonstrates good performances and applicability to actual optical networks.

articleTitle: An improved polymer digital optical switch with cross talk of -46 dB
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We present a polymer digital optical switch in which an attenuator is integrated. With the help of this an excellent cross talk (CT)) of -46 dB is obtained.

articleTitle: Real-time endless polarization tracking and control system for PMD compensation
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: A novel polarization tracking and control system for polarization-mode-dispersion (PMD) compensation is developed. The processing time of the system is reduced to several milliseconds by means of liquid crystal phase retarders and a novel polarization tracking algorithm.

articleTitle: MEMs-Tunable vertical-cavity surface-emitting lasers
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We present a MEM-VCSEL which can provide over 50 nm of wavelength tuning, up to 8 dBm optical power, and a high side mode suppression. The viability of these devices for telecom applications is directly demonstrated through transmission experiments.

articleTitle: Tunable narrow-band filters using chirped fiber Bragg gratings placed in loop mirror configuration
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: A novel simple passive narrow-band tunable filter using chirped fiber Bragg gratings in loop mirror is proposed. The filters have 3-dB bandwidth of approximately 7% of the grating bandwidth. Bandpass and notch filter characteristics are available at the device output terminals.

articleTitle: Photonic crystal fiber modelling and applications
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: Photonic crystal fibers having a microstructured air-silica cross section offer new optical properties compared to conventional fibers for telecommunication, sensor, and other applications. Recent advances within research and development of these fibers are presented.

articleTitle: Ultra low PMD fibers for long-haul high-capacity systems
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We present a new type of single mode fiber with efficiently reduced and controlled differential group delay (DGD). This task is obtained by means of spinning optimization that allows balancing of the intrinsic fiber birefringence.

articleTitle: Optical switching and its impact on optical networks
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We discuss the relationship between types of optical switch matrices, the optical crossconnects and add-drop multiplexers they are used to make, and the networks in which these elements are used.

articleTitle: Flat-top and low-loss WDM filter composed of lattice-form interleave filter and arrayed-waveguide gratings on one chip
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: A WDM filter with a 50-GHz-spacing and 102-channels was successfully fabricated by integrating two 100-GHz-spacing AWGs and a 50-GHz-spacing lattice-form interleave filter in one chip. A wide 1-dB pass-band of 30 GHz and a low-loss of 4 dB were realized.

articleTitle: Wideband frequency conversion with LiNbO/sub 3/ optical single-sideband modulator
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We demonstrated a wideband frequency conversion with a LiNbO/sub 3/ optical single-sideband modulator. The operation wavelength more than 80 nm was attained at the 10 GHz frequency conversions. No degradation in the 10 Gb/s signals was found.

articleTitle: Optical pulse train synthesis of arbitrary waveform using weight/phase-programmable 32-tapped delay line waveguide filter
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: Generation of optical pulse train of arbitrary waveform based upon Fourier spectrum synthesis is experimentally demonstrated by using a weight/phase-programmable 32-tapped delay line waveguide filter along with a frequency-tunable fiber-optic comb generator.

articleTitle: Using all-optical crossconnects in the transport network
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: Summary form only given, as follows. There has been a great deal of recent interest in all-optical switching technology. This interest has been stimulated by the emerging commercial availability of large-scale all-optical switches using MEMS (microelectromechanical systems). The high-level benefits of all-optical switching - scalability, bit-rate and protocol independence, power and footprint savings - have been articulated, but there are a number of unresolved aspects related to how these crossconnects can be deployed in a network. One option is to make the all-optical crossconnect "opaque" by surrounding it with optical-to-electrical-to-optical (OEO) converters interconnected to WDM line systems, while another option is to promote direct interoperability with WDM line systems without these converters. We explore these applications in detail with some quantification of relative economics. We also discuss how other common network functions, such as restoration, performance monitoring, and bridge-and-roll can be accomplished in a network with all-optical crossconnects.

articleTitle: High contrast waveguide devices
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: Silica-on-Si waveguides with a higher core-to-cladding index contrast can provide high-density and low-cost optical devices for photonic networks. This paper reviews recent progress on these devices focusing on arrayed waveguide gratings (AWGs) and lattice-type filters.

articleTitle: Impact of random phase errors on the performance of fiber grating dispersion compensators
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We study the impact of random phase errors on the performance of fiber grating dispersion compensators, showing analytically the correlation existing between increased fluctuations of time-delay response and the enhancement of intersymbol interference.

articleTitle: Highly reliable 1.3 /spl mu/m AlGaInAs FP lasers with low power penalty under uncooled 10 Gbps operation at 85/spl deg/C
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We have realized highly reliable 1.3 /spl mu/m AlGaInAs FP lasers with low power penalty of 1.4 dB at 10 Gbps and 85/spl deg/C. The MTTF was estimated over 1.5/spl times/10/sup 5/ hours and no deterioration of (catastrophic optical damage)COD level was observed during the life test.

articleTitle: A novel intra-cavity for efficient cascaded Raman generation using WDM couplers
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: A novel intra-cavity with a broadband spectral response is designed and demonstrated to deliver a 4th order Stokes cascaded Raman generation. A large transmission bandwidth of 295 nm is realized using the two WDM couplers. The results applied to a Raman fiber laser operating at 1706 nm wavelength using a 1313 nm pump source are reported.

articleTitle: The fabrication and modelling of non-silica microstructured optical fibres
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We present for the first time a non-silica microstructured optical fibre designed to guide light at 5 /spl mu/m using gallium lanthanum sulphide glass. We present the results of optical modelling of the structure as well as a discussion on possible applications.

articleTitle: 40Gbps optical transport system, do carriers need it?
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: Carriers have significant cost reduction expectations in deploying 40Gb/s systems. Provided that the system is well specified, taking into account the evolving nature of transport networks, 40Gb/s can deliver on the expectations.

articleTitle: Fully reconfigurable 2x2 optical cross-connect using tunable wavelength switching modules
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: Wavelength division multiplexing (WDM) not only increases fiber transmission capacity but also simplifies network operation by introducing the . optical path layer concept 111. Multi-wavelength optical cross-connects (OXC) are key elements in reconfigurable WDM networks.

articleTitle: Investigation of pump wavelength dependence of long-wavelength-band erbium-doped fiber amplifier using 1530 nm-band pump for WDM amplification
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: The 1530 nm band was investigated as a new pump wavelength band of long-wavelength-band Er/sup 3+/-doped fiber amplifier and compared with the conventional 1480 nm band. The gain coefficients of 1530 nm band pumping were two times greater than those of 1480 nm pumping.

articleTitle: Analysis of cladding-pumped L-band erbium-doped fiber amplifier performance
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: Performance of L-band cladding-pumped erbium-doped fiber amplifiers (EDFA) is numerically analyzed. It is shown, that cladding-pumping reduces build-up of short-wavelength gain and ASE power. Amplifier noise and efficiency performance can be optimized based on proper cladding area choice.

articleTitle: Influence of phase jumps in chirped fiber gratings and high-resolution interferometrical GVD characterization
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: Manufacturing of long chirped fiber gratings can lead to slight phase jumps inside the structure resulting in additional ripples in the spectrum. Simulation and high-resolution measurement results are demonstrated using a novel evaluation procedure.

articleTitle: 32 wavelength tunable mode-locked laser with 100 GHz channel spacing using an arrayed waveguide grating
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We demonstrate a discretely tunable mode-locked laser (time-to-wavelength mapped laser) consisting of a 32 wavelength silica-on-silicon planar lightwave circuit arrayed waveguide grating and an integrated electro-absorption modulator/semiconductor optical amplifier. The AWG is used to form a wavelength-dependent delay circuit to allow the oscillation wavelength to be selected by varying the modelocking frequency. The wavelength range is 1535.5-1560.5 nm, the wavelength spacing is 100 GHz, and the repetition rate is in the 10 GHz regime.

articleTitle: A novel single-fiber bidirectional optical add/drop multiplexer for distribution networks
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: A novel single-fiber bi-directional optical add/drop multiplexer is proposed for wavelength division multiplexing distribution networks. It has the advantages of low insertion loss, low cost, and providing protection function passively to the distribution ring network.

articleTitle: Optical internet architectures-application fit
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: This paper discusses how optical Internet architectures map to service-provider application spaces. This includes management and control plane considerations, client and optical layer inter-working, and transitioning to all-optical networking.

articleTitle: Single-mode non-strippable primary coated fiber
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: A single-mode nonstrippable primary coated (SM-NSP) fiber covered with a thin polymer has been successfully developed. This fiber has good mechanical and environment reliability, and can be fusion-spliced to SM fibers with low splice loss. In this report, we describe the structure and the size accuracy of an SM-NSP fiber. The mechanical reliability, the splice loss of this fiber and optical properties under various environmental conditions are also discussed.

articleTitle: Very short reach (VSR) parallel optics OC-192/STM-64 interface, optimized for network intra-PoP interconnections
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We describe the first functional, OIF approved, SONET/SDH 10Gb/s interface optimized for very short reach (VSR) - typically <300m - intra-office interconnection of routers, switches, and DWDM systems. It is a 12/spl times/1.25Gb/s channel parallel optics solution, leveraging the low cost transceiver (850nm VCSEL), and CMOS (SERDES) technologies originally developed for Gigabit Ethernet (GE).

articleTitle: Application of spread spectrum technology at 64Mcps and 2Mbps as OAM signals in transparent optical networks
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: The application of wideband spread spectrum signal at standard 2.048Mbitls and 64Mchiph on the optical carrier for the transmission of operation, administration and maintenance signals has been developed and evaluated.

articleTitle: All-optical clock frequency halving at 19.6 GHz based on period doubling in a semiconductor laser
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: All-optical clock frequency halving at 19.6 GHz is demonstrated by utilizing the nonlinear dynamics of semiconductor lasers advantageously. The quality of the frequency-divided clock signal is evaluated. Frequency-halved optical clock with a remarkably low level of phase noise (- 87 dBc/Hz @ 10 kHz offset frequency) is generated from a 19.6 GHz input optical clock. The generated clock exhibits a low phase noise over a large input frequency range of 400 MHz.

articleTitle: Convolution approach to estimates of Raman scattering in large WDM systems
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We propose a compact formulation of optical power propagation in the presence of Raman scattering which gives simple physical insight and allows faster computation of Raman scattering amongst the wavelengths of large WDM systems.

articleTitle: 3.125 Gbps 4-channel parallel optical transmitter and receiver for a very short reach 10 Gbps interface
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: A 3.125 Gbps 4-channel parallel optical transmitter and a receiver have been developed. A 12.5 Gbps throughput for a more than 300 m transmission was obtained with a package size of 15.6/spl times/45/spl times/11.4 mm/sup 3/ and a power consumption of 0.95 W.

articleTitle: A comparison between NRZ and RZ data formats with respect to PMD-induced system degradation
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We quantify the polarization-mode dispersion (PMD) induced system outage probability by means of numerical simulations for NRZ and RZ with proper comparative conditions and find that RZ performs better than NRZ. We also study the trade-off between power margin and acceptable PMD.

articleTitle: A 10-Gbit/s all-optical code generation and recognition system based on a hybrid approach of optical fiber delay line and superstructure fiber Bragg grating technologies
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We demonstrate a hybrid all-optical 160 Gchip/s encoder-decoder system based on fiber delay lines and a superstructure fiber Bragg grating (SSFBG). Our experiments confirm the possibility of using this approach in reconfigurable point-to-point optical correlation systems.

articleTitle: Economic comparison of rings and equivalent meshes of optical cross-connects assuming idealized link restoration
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: A cost comparison between various survivable optical cross-connect networks configured as single rings and equivalent meshes is described. One partial mesh provides a compromise between low cost per optical channel and low total duct distance.

articleTitle: High capacity WDM submarine systems
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: Advances in the enabling technologies for long-haul submarine systems are rapidly being transferred into commercial systems. These advances will continue to deliver massive capacity to the global telecommunications community.

articleTitle: Electroabsorption modulators monolithically integrated with semiconductor optical amplifiers for zero insertion loss utilizing InGaAs/InGaAlAs MQW material
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: Nearly zero insertion loss was obtained in 200-/spl mu/m long electroabsorption modulators by integrating 400-/spl mu/m. long semiconductor optical amplifiers with 120/spl sim/150-mA driving current. InGaAs/InGaAlAs MQW material was for the first time used in the integration.

articleTitle: 2.5 Gbps transmission over 50 km with a 1.3 /spl mu/m vertical-cavity surface-emitting laser
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We demonstrate error-free 50 km transmission at 2.5 Gbps over standard single-mode fiber using an optically pumped 1.3 /spl mu/m vertical-cavity surface-emitting laser operating at 25/spl deg/C. No optical isolator or amplification was used in the transmission demonstration.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable optical add/drop multiplexer using passive temperature-compensated wavelength tunable fiber Bragg grating
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: A reconfigurable optical add/drop multiplexer based on a passive temperature-compensated wavelength tunable fiber Bragg grating is proposed. In the temperature range, 0-70/spl deg/C, wavelength tuning range of 8 nm and wavelength tuning accuracy of 0.05 nm was attained.

articleTitle: Managed, 2R-regenerated transparent optical networking field trial spanning core and access
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We report on the successful integration of a large optical networking field trial supporting all-optical, 2R-regenerated, managed connection at 10 Gbit/s for the first time in the field, advanced protection switching schemes, and services demonstrations.

articleTitle: Experimental investigation of dispersion maps for 40/spl times/10 Gb/s transmission over 1600 km of fiber with 100-km spans employing distributed Raman amplification
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We show that system performance depends critically on the level of in-line dispersion compensation in 40/spl times/10-Gb/s WDM transmission. 110% and 90% per-span dispersion compensation yield similar high performance, however, 100% per-span dispersion compensation leads to a severe penalty.

articleTitle: Laser ablative shaping of collimator lens for single mode fiber
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: A new scheme for the phase control of optical elements using laser ablative shaping (LAS) has been developed. An ArF excimer laser was used as the light source. This method was first demonstrated with glass-plastic hybrid plates of diameter of 5 cm on a interferometer. The wavefront aberration of transmitted light was improved from 3 /spl lambda/ to /spl lambda//5 which is good enough for general purpose of optics. This LAS scheme was applied to the fabrication of micro-lens for the collimation of laser diode (LD) and single mode fiber (SMF). In these cases, the output laser beam from LD or SMF was collimated by micro-lens, and the wavefront distortion of output beam were measured by a Shack Hartmann wavefront sensor due to large wavefront aberration. The wavefront aberration of output beam from the collimation lens formed on the output surface of SMF was corrected from 15 /spl lambda/ to 2 /spl lambda/ which is very close to the actual application for the connection of SMF.

articleTitle: Self-routing of multi-terabit/sec pulses using an all-optical switch in a nonlinear coupler with dispersion flattened fiber
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: Using numerical methods we demonstrate all-optical switching and self-routing of ultrashort optical pulses in a nonlinear coupler. These ultrashort duration pulses may be suitable for operations in devices performing at multi-terabit/sec rates.

articleTitle: Demonstration of code-division multiplexing with synchronous orthogonal coding using fiber Bragg gratings
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We demonstrate two-channel synchronous code-division multiplexing using temporally orthogonal codes and fiber Bragg gratings. The use of synchronous orthogonal codes and properly gated detection permits simultaneous transmission of multiple data channels with minimal crosstalk.

articleTitle: Ultra-long haul DWDM: tool support for economic studies
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: Ultra-long haul DWDM equipment introduces exciting challenges from a tool/planning perspective. We introduce prototype tool features that support study methodology that assesses the economic applicability of mixes of several DWDM designs in a network.

articleTitle: Ultra-long-reach systems, optical transparency, and networks
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: Examines the interaction between ultra-long-reach (ULR) transmission systems, network architecture, and optical transparency. Maximal transparency requires large regenerator spacings, beyond 15000 km in North-American continental-scale networks. Smaller spacings (1000 km) can be used, at the expense of routing restrictions, or opacity. Novel network optimizations on one opaque (OPAQUE) and two partially transparent architectures (LINKOPT, NODEOPT), shows that ULR systems with spacings exceeding 1000 km are cost-effective for long-distance traffic on sparse continental backbones. Rings with OADM's can benefit from higher spacings.

articleTitle: Dispersion measurement of chirped fiber Bragg gratings using loop mirror configuration
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: A novel scheme for measuring the dispersion of chirped fiber Bragg gratings is demonstrated using loop mirror configuration. The technique is relatively simple and requires only a broadband light source.

articleTitle: 1 Tb/s (40 Gb/s/spl times/25 channel) DWDM quasi-DM soliton transmission over 1,500 km using dispersion-managed single-mode fiber and conventional C-band EDFAs
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We report a 1 Tb/s (40 Gb/s/spl times/25 channel) dense WDM quasi-DM soliton transmission over 1,500 km with the use of a dispersion-managed single-mode fiber. The spectral efficiency was as high as 0.4 b/s/Hz. The transmission line comprised conventional 1.3 /spl mu/m single-mode fibers and dispersion compensating fibers with dispersion slope compensation and a repeater span of 50 km.

articleTitle: Distributed provisioning of wavelength channels in multi-service WDM networks
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We propose a distributed protocol for wavelength channel provisioning in WDM networks, where the network state information, related to transmission quality, reliability, manageability and traffic conditions, is based on an autonomous and service-differentiated characterisation of optical network elements.

articleTitle: Performance of a liquid-crystal optical harmonic equalizer
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We present an optical gain equalization approach using all-optical liquid-crystal devices and the harmonic synthesis approach. The functionality of optical harmonic equalizers (OHEs) is to dynamically adjust the gain profiles of optical amplifiers (EDFAs) by generating required transfer functions with a series of variable harmonic filters.

articleTitle: Chromatic and polarization mode dispersion compensation using spectral holography
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: A new adaptive method for accomplishing both chromatic and polarization mode dispersion compensation on parallel DWDM fibers is proposed based on the third order nonlinear technique of coherent transient spectral holography.

articleTitle: Demonstration of demultiplexing in high speed OTDM systems using a two photon absorption based switch
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: A demultiplexer based on two-photon absorption in a commercial laser diode has been used to demonstrate essentially error free switching and detection of individual channels from an 80 Gbit/s optical-time-division-multiplexed data stream.

articleTitle: Dynamic gain flattening of an erbium-doped fiber amplifier using a high-birefringence fiber loop mirror
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: A flexible method based on a high-birefringence fiber loop mirror is proposed for the gain flattening of an erbium-doped fiber amplifier. The gain profile was flattened to within /spl plusmn/0.9 dB over a 33 nm bandwidth.

articleTitle: Q-factor improvement in a jitter limited optical RZ system using nonlinearity of normal dispersion fiber placed at receiver
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We adopted a new detection scheme using nonlinearity of normal dispersion fiber in a jitter limited 10 Gb/s soliton transmission. The obtained amplitude margin at BER of 10/sup -9/ was three times larger than the conventional sheme.

articleTitle: Measurements and simulations of intersymbol interference penalty in new high speed 50 /spl mu/m multimode fiber links operating at 10 Gb/s
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: Our measurements and simulations demonstrate robust 10 Gb/s data transmission exceeding 300 m, using a new high-speed 50 /spl mu/m multimode fiber. The results can be used to broaden the component specification range for 10 Gigabit Ethernet applications.

articleTitle: Optimum dispersion of non-zero dispersion shifted fiber for high bit rate DWDM systems
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: Simulations reveal that the optimum dispersion of the transmission fiber lies around +8 to +12 ps/nm/km in dense WDM transmission with a channel spacing of 50 GHz. Experiments using fibers fabricated with various dispersions support the calculations.

articleTitle: 640 Gb/s (32/spl times/20 gb/s) WDM transmission with 0.4 (bit/s)/Hz spectral efficiency using short-period dispersion managed fiber (Perfect Cable/sup TM/)
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We demonstrate 640 Gb/s (32 ch/spl times/20 Gb/s) WDM transmission with 0.4 (bit/s)/Hz spectral efficiency using short-period dispersion-managed fiber (Perfect Cable/sup TM/). The average Q-factor was measured to be better than 18 dB after transmission over 280 km.

articleTitle: 40 GHz all-optical shift register with semiconductor optical amplifiers for switching and feedback
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We report for the first time the operation of an all-optical digital processing circuit based entirely on semiconductor optical amplifiers (SOAs). SOAs are used both for the nonlinear element in an interferometer and for the feedback amplifier. A 40 GHz all-optical shift register with inverter is demonstrated in which the feedback amplifier is also a SOA. This is a key advance since it proves the feasibility of constructing truly low latency all-optical signal processing circuits. It brings closer the prospect of performing high-speed processing 'on-the-fly' in future photonic networks.

articleTitle: Dispersion division multiplexing technique for doubling the spectral efficiency of subcarrier multiplexed data transmission over fiber optical links
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We demonstrate a novel all-optical multiplexing technique for doubling the data rate in subcarrier-multiplexed transmission over optical fiber by taking advantage of dispersion-induced power fading at the subcarrier frequency.

articleTitle: Proposal and demonstration of transmission of 10 Gb/s over 300 m of installed-base 62.5 /spl mu/m multimode fibre using advanced modulation formats
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We demonstrate that by using a combination of duobinary modulation and simultaneous baseband and subcarrier modulated channels, an installed base 62.5 /spl mu/m MMF can support high quality (<1 dB penalty) transmission of 10 Gb/s over 300 m.

articleTitle: New theoretical model of ytterbium-doped double-clad fiber for laser application
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We present a new analytical model which allows to model a double clad fiber amplifier or a laser. Comparison with experimental results using a sided pumping scheme with a double clad ytterbium -doped fibre laser is performed. We present a new analytical model which allows to model an amplifier or a laser using a DCF. The multimode pump is modeled by a equivalent source term launched in the single core of the DCF. It leads to an analytical model comparable to a single mode fiber model. We use it to calculate the evolution of the amplified spontaneous emission (ASE) along the fiber, and find out the optimum fiber length for laser operation.

articleTitle: Comparison of switching windows of an all-optical 160 Gbit/s demultiplexer with base data rates of 10 Gbit/s and 40 Gbit/s
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We compare theoretical and experimental switching windows of an all-optical switch designed for demultiplexing of 160 Gbit/s to 10 Gbit/s and 40 Gbit/s. Demultiplexing to 40 Gbit/s reduces the transmittance of the switch but improves the cross-talk performance.

articleTitle: High output power erbium doped waveguide amplifier for QAM distribution
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We report on the first Er/sup 3+/-Yb/sup 3+/ doped planar waveguide amplifier with +14 dBm output power which we use as a post-amplifier for the DWDM transmission of eight wavelengths, each carrying 35 6-MHz 64-QAM channels, over an unrepeated span of 175 km.

articleTitle: Short pulse and low noise actively mode-locked 10 GHz semiconductor laser with a fiber Bragg grating external cavity
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: Using a semiconductor laser with a fiber Bragg grating external cavity, 10 GHz actively mode-locked short pulses (3.8 ps) with very low timing jitter (160 fs RMS) have been generated at a wavelength of 1553 nm.

articleTitle: Full optical spectral utilization by microwave domain filtering of tandem single sidebands
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We present an optical tandem single sideband receiver that eliminates the need for guardbands between adjacent WDM channels, while also receiving signals that have different data on the two sidebands of the same optical carrier.

articleTitle: A smart layer two protocol for IP over WDM
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: A layer two protocol for Internet protocol (IP) over WDM transport is presented. It supports operation and maintenance of wide area networks by means of dedicated messages. Its state machine for robust synchronization is described. A new layer two protocol tailored to the needs of IP over WDM transport has been presented which features OAM support for wide area networks (WANs) and robust synchronization. Bringing IP and WDM closer together it has the potential to reduce overall network cost and to simplify network management. The proof that it works as expected has been done by successful operation of a demonstrator.

articleTitle: Novel scheme for efficient and cost-effective forwarding of packets in optical networks without header modification
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We present a novel scheme for addressing the outputs in optical packet switches and demonstrate its good scalability. The scheme requires neither header modification nor distribution of routing information to the packet switches, thus reducing optical component count while simplifying network management.

articleTitle: A robust and flexible all optical CDMA multichannel transmission system for the access domain
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: A multichannel optical CDMA system for the access domain, which is fully variable in terms of channel data rate and channel number is presented. Various network functionalities are illustrated, which are completely realized on the optical layer.

articleTitle: SNR improvement in EDFA repeaters using cascaded optical fiber grating couplers
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: A configuration for SNR improvement by reducing ASE noise in EDFA repeaters for WDM signals using cascaded optical fiber grating couplers (FGCs) is proposed. The effectiveness of the configuration is experimentally demonstrated and discussed.

articleTitle: Acoustics-induced mode coupling for reflection wavelength switching in a tapered fiber Bragg grating
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: Experimental and theoretical results of reflection wavelength variation in a tapered fiber Bragg grating, induced by an applied acoustic wave for generating micro bending and hence controlling the phase-matching condition, are reported.

articleTitle: A 8/spl times/8 all optical space-switch based on a novel 8/spl times/1 MOEMS switching module
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We report a 8/spl times/8 switch based on a novel MOEMS technology allowing wide bandwidth (1300-1650 nm), fast switching (<1 ms), excellent isolation (>50 dB) and high modularity. This switch allow the realization of high capacity optical cross-connects (e.g.1024/spl times/lO24).

articleTitle: The impact of polarization-mode dispersion on four-wave wave mixing in WDM systems
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: The impact of polarization-mode dispersion (PMD) on four-wave mixing (FWM) is evaluated. A simple model is developed from the FWM transfer function on polarization states of the signals. The implications of the results on the orthogonal polarization launch scheme for WDM systems are also investigated.

articleTitle: Large second-harmonic generation in thermally poled silica waveguides
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We report the observation of very large second-harmonic signals from thermally poled silica waveguide samples. Secondary ion mass spectrometry measurements show that significant amounts of silver ions are injected from the top electrode during poling.

articleTitle: Accelerated testing of liquid crystal components for use in optical networking devices
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: Liquid crystal components developed for optical networking devices were exposed to accelerated environments. These components survived the equivalent of 22dBm/channel. Contrast ratio was stable at the 40dB level after 1250 hours of 85/85 exposure.

articleTitle: Terabit DWDM systems: a service provider's view of drivers and features
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: The drivers that cause a service provider to select a new terabit DWDM system can get lost in the noise of "bigger, longer, faster". The paper describes a service provider's view of these drivers.

articleTitle: Distributed photonic A/D conversion using a neural network, oversampling, and spectral noise shaping
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: An array of low-resolution quantizers embedded in a distributed mesh architecture is shown to provide improved performance while reducing the effects of component mismatch. A photonic approach is described which incorporates a modelocked laser, interferometer, and a smart pixel array.

articleTitle: Multi-terabit/s DWDM; technologies and perspectives
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: The current research status for DWDM systems are summarized here in the light of 3.2 Tb/s and 6.4 Tb/s transmission experiments, and future directions are discussed with respect to the practical use of multi-terabit/s system and to technical advances required for further increases in capacity.

articleTitle: Observation of fundamental mode cut-off at short wavelength in a holey optical fiber
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We have observed that fundamental mode is cut-off at short wavelengths in a standard holey optical fiber (HOF), while the same fiber guides light at long wavelengths. This can be an another evidence that the guiding mechanism in a holey optical fiber is mostly due to average index effect rather than photonic bandgap effect. This strange property of a HOF can be potentially useful for device applications.

articleTitle: Long-term planning of optical networks
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We present novel methodologies (based on stochastic traffic modelling, robust and multi-period optimisation) to cope with the fast technological innovations and increasing degree of uncertainty during the long-term planning of optical networks.

articleTitle: Optical switching and routing
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: A fully reconfigurable 2/spl times/2 optical cross-connect using tunable wavelength switching module is presented. A modular tunable wavelength switching module is proposed and used to construct 2/spl times/2 fully reconfigurable optical crossconnects. Large size optical switch use is avoided in the OXC and it is easy to upgrade to more wavelength channels.

articleTitle: Multi-channel power level monitor with upward-reflector and sensor-array integrated in planar lightwave circuit
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: A novel type of in-line multi-channel monitor module with compact packaging has been developed. This module has low polarization sensitivity (PDL:0.13 dB, polarization dependent monitoring sensitivity: 0.2 dB), and is applicable to various WDM components.

articleTitle: The impact of PMD on nonlinear interchannel crosstalk in DWDM transoceanic systems
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: The impact of PMD coupled with nonlinear interaction in long-haul DWDM system was numerically studied. We show that in certain regimes of channel spacing and PMD, orthogonal launch of adjacent channels provides significant performance improvement.

articleTitle: Less than 36pm wavelength drift over [0-50/spl deg/C] range with low-cost plug and play lasers with a-thermal wavelength selection in the connector
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: A new low-cost, thermally compensated, versatile, external cavity fiber grating lasers in a plastic module shows output power above 1 mW and a wavelength stability within 36 pm over 0-50/spl deg/C. Low penalty transmission is achieved over C-band.

articleTitle: Soliton self-frequency shift in a short tapered air-silica microstructure fiber
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We report soliton self-frequency shift over the communications window from 1.3 /spl mu/m to 1.65 /spl mu/m in a tapered air-silica microstructure fiber as short as 15 cm. The frequency shift is intensity-dependent, enabling novel telecommunications applications.

articleTitle: Dispersion-managed solitons for 160 Gbit/s transmission
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: The use of dispersion-managed (DM) solitons for 160 Gbit/s data transmission over 1000 km in fiber lines where the period of dispersion-management is much shorter than the amplifier spacing is investigated through numerical simulations.

articleTitle: 1.3 /spl mu/m tapered DFB lasers for isolator-free 2.5 Gbits all-optical networks
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: All-optical networks require low cost and high efficiency laser sources. We demonstrate floorless 2.5 Gbit/s transmission under 20 dB return loss with 1.3 /spl mu/m tapered lasers designed for optics-free, isolator-free modules with no temperature control.

articleTitle: Anamorphic and aspheric microlenses and microlens arrays for telecommunication applications
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: A wafer-based fabrication process used to produce surface-relief microlenses for telecommunication applications is presented. Anamorphic and aspheric collimating lens profiles can be achieved, and samples have been measured to achieve insertion losses less than 0.2 dB/pair.

articleTitle: Suppression of collision-induced timing jitter in WDM RZ-pulse transmission by adjustment of decision timing
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: Effectiveness of bitwise adjustment of decision timing at receiver in suppressing collision-induced timing jitter in dispersion-managed WDM RZ-pulse transmission is numerically analyzed. Influence of imperfect adjustment of decision timing is examined.

articleTitle: Measuring poling-induced nonlinearities in Ge:SiON waveguides using a Bragg grating
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: Thermal poling of a Bragg grating provides an excellent way of determining poling induced nonlinear effects in glass waveguides. We report nonlinear coefficients for negative thermal poling along with the induced dc electric field.

articleTitle: QAM-PON and super PON for access distribution networks
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We propose a passive optical network (PON) system based on quadrature amplitude modulated (QAM) sub-carrier multiplexing (SCM) of 53 6 MHz 64/256-QAM channels. Sensitivities of -22 dBm and -17.5 dBm are achieved over 51 km of fiber under full duplex and broadcast delivery to 128 nodes for 64 and 256 QAM, respectively.

articleTitle: Broadcasting a single wavelength over a WDM network
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We propose and demonstrate a wavelength-division-multiplexed network in which one wavelength is used for broadcast signals, while other wavelengths are used for switched signals. A novel device-the Bragg tap-is demonstrated.

articleTitle: 40 Gbit/s 25 WDM RZ signal transmission using L-band amplifiers and NZ-DSF spans
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: 40 Gbit/s 25 WDM RZ signal transmission over 550 km was demonstrated using L-band amplifiers and non-zero dispersion shifted fibers, and transmission impairments were reduced by effective dispersion management. The Q factor obtained on average was 15.4 dB after transmission.

articleTitle: Nonlinear properties of dispersion management modules employing high-order mode fibers
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: Dispersion management modules based on large effective area, relatively short, high-order mode fibers, are shown to have high tolerance to optical nonlinear effects, thereby allowing both dispersion and slope compensation without significant input power limitations.

articleTitle: A new ATM PON system suitable for local access and local private networking services
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: An N/spl times/N star coupler and N optical network units with a circulator and two fiber Bragg gratings were employed to form a fully transparent, 155 Mb/s optical star network over the existing asynchronous transfer mode (ATM) passive optical network (PON) system.

articleTitle: High-speed electroabsorption (EA) modulator modules using the flip-chip bonding (FCB) technique
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We developed EA-modulator modules with over 40-GHz modulation bandwidth using the flip-chip bonding (FCB) technique. The FCB minimizes parasitic inductance and module-to-module variation in electrical characteristics, and is indispensable to high-speed EA-modulator modules for 80 Gbit/s.

articleTitle: Bidirectional add/drop amplifier module with a single dispersion compensating fiber module
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We propose a new bidirectional add/drop amplifier (BADA) module to halve the dispersion compensation cost. We successfully demonstrate the bidirectional transmission and add/drop function of 10 Gb/s /spl times/ 14 channels over 200-km of SMF by using the BADA module.

articleTitle: 20 Gbit/s directly modulated 1310 nm ridge laser
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: A 20 Gbit/s directly modulated laser is demonstrated at 1310 nm. MOCVD growth combined with a ridge waveguide design have the potential for a low cost short reach solution at bit rates greater than 10 Gbit/s.

articleTitle: A study on WDM network architectures for Internet backbone networks in Korea
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We estimated transmission circuits demand for Internet traffic in Korea and performed economic analysis of several WDM network architectures for accommodating the estimated demand. About 20 WDM nodes are sufficient to support the demand effectively.

articleTitle: Erbium lanthanum co-doped fiber for L-band amplifier with high efficiency, low non-linearity and low NF
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We have developed an erbium/lanthanum doped fibre (ELDF) that has high Er concentration, and which attained high efficiency without quenching. We demonstrated that the ELDF had high gain per length, low non-linearity at L-band, and low noise figure compared to conventional EDF.

articleTitle: High-efficiency broadband supercontinuum generation centered at 1483.4 nm using Raman fiber laser
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: High-efficiency broadband (1434-1527 nm) continuous-wave supercontinuum with average power of 2. 1 W is obtained when 350 m singlemode fiber and 50% feedback fiber Bragg grating at 1484 nm were spliced to 2.22 W/1483.4 nm Raman fiber laser.

articleTitle: Two-fiber optical channel shared protection ring with 4/spl times/4 thermal-optic switches
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: A two-fiber optical channel shared protection ring including node architecture, signaling protocol, control hardware and software is designed and implemented experimentally. A total protection switching time of 12 ms is demonstrated, along with a revert-to-normal switching time of 3 ms.

articleTitle: PMD in single-mode fibers: measurements of local birefringence correlation length
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We report measurements of birefringence correlation length performed on long single-mode telecommunication fibers. The proposed technique is based on a polarization sensitive backscattering analysis. Results are consistent with standard differential group delay measurement.

articleTitle: 160 Gbit/s OCDM/WDM (10 Gbit/s/spl times/4 CDM/spl times/4 WDM) transmission with a novel side-lobes suppression detection
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: A novel side-lobes suppression detection based on passive balanced detection with half-inverse BPSK-code sets is introduced to suppress interference noise of 10 Gbit/s optical code division multiplexing (OCDM) system. 10 Gbit/s/spl times/4 CDM/spl times/4 WDM over 80 km transmission is demonstrated for the first time.

articleTitle: A nonsymmetrical Mach-Zehnder interferometer for suppressing pattern effect in SOAs
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: A novel idea of using change in index of refraction to suppress the pattern effect caused by gain variation in saturated semiconductor optical amplifiers (SOAs) with Mach-Zehnder interferometers is demonstrated. The principle and the experimental verification are presented.

articleTitle: Thermo-optic 1/spl times/2- and 1/spl times/8-vertical coupled switches (VCS) using hybrid polymer/silica integration technology
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: Thermo-optic 1/spl times/2-vertical coupled switches (VCS) were fabricated using a polymer/ silica integration technology. The switches exhibited low insertion loss (<1.5 dB), low crosstalk (<-32 dB), low switching power (/spl sim/80 mW), and polarisation independence. Based on this building block, a 1/spl times/8-VCS has been demonstrated.

articleTitle: Low power electrochromic variable optical attenuator with 50dB attenuation range
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: A variable optical attenuator based upon a new molybdenum electrochromic compound is described. The device exhibits an attenuation range of >50dB at 1310nm, for a drive power of 150/spl mu/W, and an insertion loss of 1.5dB.

articleTitle: Wavelength references for 1300 nm and L-band WDM
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We have surveyed potential references for 1300 nm and L-band wavelength calibration. We have developed a 1314 nm methane reference for our internal calibration and are developing a carbon-monoxide transfer standard for the 1560-1630 nm region.

articleTitle: Testing passive DWDM components: uncertainties in swept-wavelength measurement systems
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We discuss intrinsic compromises between measurement speed and accuracy of swept wavelength measurement systems. Side-effects from reducing measurement accuracy are demonstrated and explained. Setup precautions and post-processing improvements are suggested.

articleTitle: Semi-analytical modeling and design tool for WDM RZ systems. Validation results
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We have developed semi-analytical tools to model and design long-haul dispersion-managed WDM RZ systems. Our approach provides a drastic speed-up of system budgeting compared to conventional modeling based on split-step methods. We have validated our analytical models experimentally and numerically.

articleTitle: A new modal power distribution measurement for high-speed laser transmitters
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We propose and demonstrate a new technique for measuring the modal power distribution of light launched into a multimode fiber. When applied to high-speed lasers our method is much simpler than existing ones.

articleTitle: Waveguiding at 1550 nm using photonic crystal structures in silicon on insulator wafers
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: Design, fabrication and light guiding in planar photonic crystal structures including sharp corners with a bending radius less than 1 micron are demonstrated at 1550 nm wavelength in silicon waveguides on silicon dioxide substrates. Photon confinement in the sample plane was achieved by a photonic crystal structure while confinement in the vertical direction was achieved by index of refraction contrast.

articleTitle: Microresonator devices for DWDM systems
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: Filters and switches for integrated DWDM subsystems using microresonators vertically coupled to waveguides are described. High Q resonator/waveguides components are fabricated by double-sided processing using wafer bonding. Tunable laser and detector designs are described.

articleTitle: Wavelength conversion with no pattern effect at 40 Gbps using an electroabsorption waveguide as a phase modulator
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: This is the first report on a wavelength converter utilizing cross-phase modulation in a semiconductor electroabsorption waveguide. We have successfully demonstrated 40 Gbps wavelength conversion with no dependence on the pattern length owing to a fast absorption recovery in the electroabsorption waveguide.

articleTitle: Recent status of perfluorinated graded index plastic optical fiber and its novel termination method
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We report recent progress in perfluorinated graded index plastic optical fiber and its operability with a gigabit Ethernet transceiver designed for silica glass fiber. An easy termination method and connector are also mentioned.

articleTitle: Limits on the spectral efficiency of intensity modulated direct detection systems with optical amplifiers
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We study the information capacity and the spectral efficiency of communication systems with optical amplifiers, in the direct detection intensity modulation case. We show that with typical values of OSNR of the order of 20 dB, multilevel signaling can increase the spectral efficiency by no more than a factor of 3.5 relative to binary modulated systems. The highest spectral efficiency is obtained with a symmetric optical spectrum, and it cannot be improved by removing one sideband as in the single sideband modulation case.

articleTitle: Photonic lightwave circuits
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: Summary form only given. Photonic lightwave circuits are optical devices comprised of waveguides and sometimes active devices, such as phase shifters, amplifiers, or modulators. This field is immense, including devices from electroabsorption modulated lasers to acoustooptic wavelength add-drops. Because of the limited time, we have chosen to focus on arrayed-waveguide-based and a few other interferometer-based devices. This includes multi/demultiplexers, dynamic gain equalization filters, wavelength add-drops, dispersion compensators, switches, and optical regenerators. It has been claimed for a long time now that photonic lightwave circuits should be cheaper to build in large quantities than their bulls counterparts and thus capture the marketplace. We also discuss cases where this has and has not happened.

articleTitle: Fabrication and heat treatment effects on absorption characteristics of glass fibers doped with PbTe semiconductor quantum dots
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: PbTe doped glass fibers for nonlinear optical application were developed using a modified solution doping method in the MCVD process. An absorption peak near 1050 nm was observed and which was attributed to optical resonance due to PbTe quantum dots precipitated in the core of the fiber. The effect of heat treatment on the absorption peak position and absorption intensity was also investigated.

articleTitle: All-optical passive regeneration of 40 Gbit/s soliton data stream using dispersion management and in-line nonlinear optical loop mirrors
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We numerically demonstrate for the first time that dispersion management and in-line nonlinear optical loop mirrors can achieve all-optical passive regeneration and distance-unlimited transmission of a soliton data stream at 40 Gbit/s over standard fibre.

articleTitle: Error-free coherent detection of OC-192 phase-modulated data using phase-to-amplitude conversion (PAC) based on optical injection locking
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We propose a novel coherent detection technique without phase locked loops (PLL). In this technique, phase-to-amplitude conversion based on injection-locking is performed. We demonstrate the error-free detection for OC-192 (9.95328Gb/s) phase-modulated data without serious laser phase noise problems.

articleTitle: Role of power jitter induced by interchannel interactions in dispersion-managed lines
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: Collision induced power jitter is examined in dispersion-managed wavelength-division-multiplexed transmission systems. The power jitter causes a serious problem for a singly-periodic dispersion managed line having almost zero average dispersion, which can be reduced by applying doubly-periodic dispersion management.

articleTitle: MPLS and GMPLS: Everything you didn't want to know
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: Summary form only given. Generalized Multi Protocol Label Switching (GMPLS) refers to the standardized application of MPLS control plane concepts for general connection provisioning in multiple technology domains, such as optical and SONET/SDH networks. GMPLS extends MPLS label-switched path establishment techniques to address the establishment of lightpaths, SONET/SDH trails, etc. This tutorial describes the principles of the MPLS control plane and how they are generalized in GMPLS. The application of GMPLS in optical and SONET/SDH networks, and features not presently covered by GMPLS are also described.

articleTitle: 1.22 Tbit/s WDM transmission over 7,221 km with 38 nm bandwidth expanded by distributed Raman amplifier and EDFA
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: By using a signal bandwidth expansion combined with a distributed Raman amplifier and an EDFA, we have achieved WDM transmission over 7,221 km at 1.22 Tbit/s in the L-band alone. The scheme seems to be more practical because it has relatively low loss gain equalization, the shorter wavelength OSNR improvement, and effective gain tilt compensation.

articleTitle: The electric field switching in resonant, tunneling diode electroabsorption modulator
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: A resonant tunneling diode(RTD) can be imbedded in an optical waveguide to produce a new type of integrated optoelectronic device which integrates an electronic amplifier with a waveguide electroabsorption modulator (EAM). The device is called the RTD-EAM and it is particularly well suited to high-speed, low voltage, digital operation. An expression for the magnitude of the electric field switching is derived and compared with an experimental measurement of the Franz-Keldysh band-edge shift at 1550 nm of the InAlGaAs semiconductor employed to form the optical waveguide; agreement to within 12% is obtained.

articleTitle: Figure-eight fiber laser by using a dispersion-imbalanced nonlinear optical loop mirror with lumped dispersive elements
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: Mode locking of a figure-eight fiber laser using a dispersion-imbalanced nonlinear optical loop mirror with lumped dispersive elements is demonstrated for the first time. The modelocked pulses show noise-like properties whose pulse width and average optical power are 3.26 ns and 6.526 mW respectively when 95 mW pump power is provided at 980 nm wavelength.

articleTitle: Multiple-output Er/sup 3+/ fiber amplifier for analog and QAM distribution systems
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We describe the performance of a low noise and high power four-output Er/sup 3+/-Yb/sup 3+/ fiber amplifier for the distribution of analog video and data signals. Successful fiber transmission links of 77 NTSC analog CATV channels and 34 6 MHz 64-QAM channels are demonstrated.

articleTitle: FWM noise reduction in bursty metro transmission
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We analyze the occurrence of FWM. noise in bursty metro network transmission of Ethernet packets directly on the WDM layer. We obtain more than 5 dB reduction in FWM noise for traffic loads less than 0.7 both for uniform and self-similar traffic.

articleTitle: Optimisation of optical receiver for 10 Gbit/s optical duobinary transmission system
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: Optimisation of a receiver for an optical duobinary signal is studied numerically. It is shown that a conventional receiver is not optimum neither when a DCF is used before the receiver nor without a DCF being used. The optimum receiver for an optical duobinary system is identified.

articleTitle: Performance of unamplified access optical network using broad band coupler architecture
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We demonstrate and report results for a seven node optical network for metro application. The ring architecture is unamplified and uses broadband couplers for low cost and improved flexibility. Here we have demonstrated seven nodes plus a hub node for 2.5 Gb/s signals, which suggests that a five or six nodes system may be practical. For 10 Gb/s signals, 4 to 5 nodes are practical given a directly modulated laser source and avalanche photodiode (APD) photodetectors.

articleTitle: Polarization insensitive adaptive gain profile equalizer using variable Faraday rotators and walk-off crystals
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We propose novel adaptive gain profile equalizer using variable Faraday rotators and walk-off crystal. Gain flatness of the EDFA with which it is used in a simple configuration is maintained to less than 1.2 dB over an input dynamic range of 10 dB.

articleTitle: Dual-wavelength cascaded Raman fiber laser
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We have demonstrated a stable and tunable dual-wavelength Raman fiber laser which can be used as a pump source for hybrid type and gain controlled C- and L-band distributed Raman and lumped erbium doped fiber amplifier. A long period grating is used to suppress the gain competition between the two wavelength laser modes and prevent the high order Stokes oscillation. Intensity and wavelength tuning of the two lasing modes at 1480 nm and 1500 nm are achieved by tuning one and both of the fiber grating used in the laser cavity, respectively.

articleTitle: Polarization insensitive optical amplifiers in AlInGaAs
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: Optical gain calculations have been performed for polarization insensitive amplifiers in AlInGaAs/InP for both 1300 nm and 1550 nm windows. Amplifiers, fabricated and tested at 1300 nm, show less than 0.3 dB gain difference between TE and TM modes.

articleTitle: 16-channel 40 Gb/s carrier-suppressed RZ ETDM/DWDM transmission over 720 km NDSF without polarisation channel interleaving
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We report experimental and simulation results on transmission. and simultaneous dispersion-compensation of 16/spl times/40 Gb/s carrier-suppressed RZ ETDM signals with 0.4 bit/s/Hz spectral-efficiency over 6/spl times/120 km NDSF. Q-factors between 16.3 and 17.7 dB were achieved at 2/sup 31/-1 pattern length without FEC or polarisation interleaving.

articleTitle: Long-distance analog links
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: In preparation for using in-ground fiber optics for wideband antenna remoting, measurements of analog link performance have been made over Bossnet. Over a distance of 570 km, >20 GHz of bandwidth is measured with a spur-free dynamic range of 90 dB-Hz/sup 2/3/.

articleTitle: Amplitude noise and timing jitter of pulses generated by supercontinuum spectrum-slicing for data-regeneration and TDM/WDM applications
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We numerically investigate the amplitude-noise and the timing jitter of pulses obtained by slicing coherent supercontinuum spectra. Applications such as TDM/WDM systems and all-optical data regeneration are addressed. We discuss system parameters for optimizing the quality of sliced pulses.

articleTitle: The effect of SPM, EPM and sign of dispersion on the second order distortion in analog link
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We present a complete physical understanding of the role of self phase modulation (SPM), external phase modulation (EPM) and the sign of dispersion on the second order distortion generated by non-linear propagation in a 1550nm externally modulated analog link. We show that the distortion generated by SPM can be compensated using the proper EPM parameters.

articleTitle: Integrated shim layer
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: The integrated shim layer hides the implementation details of optical transport systems. It performs framing, setting up and tearing down lightpaths, performance monitoring, and localized protection switching. It resides in the optical layer as the driver module.

articleTitle: Enhanced Kerr effect experienced by ASE light
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: A surprisingly high fiber optic Kerr coefficient for amplified spontaneous emission has been measured through self-phase modulation. This enhancement originates from the dependence of two-photon absorption rate on the second-order degree of coherence of light.

articleTitle: Demultiplexing of 80 Gbit/s pulse-position modulated data with an ultrafast nonlinear interferometer
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We demonstrate all-optical demultiplexing of an 80 Gbit/s pulse-position modulated data stream using an ultrafast nonlinear interferometer.
