Use of pulse-position modulated data permits a novel switch design that performs simultaneous demultiplexing, modulation-format conversion, and wavelength conversion.

articleTitle: 25 GHz interleaved bidirectional transmission over non-zero dispersion shifted fiber
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We demonstrate error-free 25 GHz interleaved bidirectional OC-192 transmission of 40+40 channels over five 80 km spans of non-zero dispersion shifted fiber. Simultaneous suppression of four-wave mixing and Rayleigh backscatter is achieved in ultradense bidirectional architecture.

articleTitle: Frequency response metrology for high-speed optical receivers
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We use "standard" optical sources along with microwave calibration methods to accurately calibrate optical receivers to 50 GHz and beyond. The calibrated receivers can be used to characterize sources and receivers using common electrical instrumentation.

articleTitle: Dispersion flat and low non-linear optical link with new type of reverse dispersion fiber (RDF-60)
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: New type of reverse dispersion fiber (RDF-60) has been developed successfully. Totally flat line in a wide band could be obtained by connecting RDF-60 with SMF. RDF-60 had large dispersion as -60 ps/nm/km and A/sub eff/ as large as conventional RDF, so low non-linearity could be realized.

articleTitle: 60 Gbit/s WDM-OTDM transmultiplexing using an electro-absorption modulator
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We propose a WDM-OTDM transmultiplexing technique to generate a stable high speed OTDM signal with adjustable pulse width by using an electro-absorption modulator and demonstrate 60 Gbit/s signal generation from three 20 Gbit/s WDM signals.

articleTitle: Performance monitoring of optical networks with synchronous and asynchronous sampling
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: Experimental measurements are made for two approaches to performance monitoring of signals in optical networks. The techniques are bit error ratio (BER) estimation by synchronous and asynchronous sampling, respectively, and we compare their performance with different signal impairments.

articleTitle: Metro network architecture scenarios, equipment requirements and implications for carriers
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: Metropolitan network traffic demands are used to project network topology and element characteristics assuming several different market penetrations for existing (ILEC) and new (CLEC) carriers.

articleTitle: The direction of optical technology in the metro area
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: In metro networks, explosive, unpredictable bandwidth demands continue to be the norm. Optical solutions are the best answer, but with SONET rings still ubiquitous - "all optical" architectures are still a ways off. For now, carriers need optical solutions that coexist with SONET while evolving toward more flexible - and ultimately all-optical - models.

articleTitle: 3.08 Tb/s (77/spl times/42.7 Gb/s) transmission over 1200 km of non-zero dispersion-shifted fiber with 100-km spans using C and L-band distributed Raman amplification
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: In this paper, we demonstrate, for the first time, transmission of 3.08 Tb/s (77/spl times/42.7 Gb/s) over 1200 km fiber with 100 km spans by employing dual C- and L-band distributed Raman amplification, experimental low dispersion slope TrueWave/sup (R)/ fiber, and forward error correction. The 3.08 Tb/s is comprised of forty 100 GHz spaced WDM channels in the C-band and thirty-seven 100 GHz spaced WDM channels in the L-band. Error free transmission of all 77 channels is achieved. Furthermore, low dispersion slope fiber and matched dispersion-compensating fiber (DCF) alleviate the need for any per-channel post-compensation in the C-band.

articleTitle: A high-efficiency power-stable three-wavelength configurable Raman fiber laser
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: :A highly efficient configurable three-wavelength cascaded Raman laser suitable for broadband Raman amplification is demonstrated. The power at each wavelength is adjusted by varying the reflectivity of fiber grating output couplers. Measurements of the power stability at each wavelength show that the source is stable.

articleTitle: The measurement of fast state of polarization changes in aerial fiber
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: The state of polarization was measured of an aerial fiber over a six-day period. An upper limit of the state of polarization changes in aerial fiber was observed as 1.824 seconds. This gave an indication of how fast the polarization mode dispersion changes.

articleTitle: Arrayed waveguide grating DWDM interleaver
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: Arrayed waveguide grating DWDM interleavers are proposed and analyzed. With simple design rules, interleavers with low channel cross-talk and flat-top passband can be easily implemented.

articleTitle: Bandwidth limitations of broadband distributed Raman fiber amplifiers for WDM systems
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: Pump interactions have been identified as a limiting factor for the gain bandwidth product of broadband distributed Raman fiber amplifiers. With respect to distributed Raman gain, it is more advantageous to add WDM channels at wavelengths above C+L band rather than below.

articleTitle: High optical power testing of physical contact connectors at 1550 nm
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We have investigated the high optical power handling capability of standard SC physical contact (PC) and angled physical contact (APC) connectors using SMF-28/sup TM/ fiber at powers of 1 and 3 W at 1550 nm. We will report results of short-term exposure tests of mated connector pairs prepared with various endface surface conditions.

articleTitle: S-band fiber optic amplifiers
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: This paper reviews S-band fiber optic amplifiers including thulium-doped fiber amplifiers (TDFA), gain-shifted thulium-doped fiber amplifiers and Raman amplifiers describe TDFA, gain shifted (GS) TDFA and Raman amplifiers. The TDFAs or GS-TDFA seem to have a slight advantage over Raman amplifiers in terms of power conversion efficiency, but we must make further improvements in power conversion efficiency if we wish to employ all these amplifiers under practical conditions.

articleTitle: Joint IP/optical layer restoration after a router failure
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: The optical layer can provide for an Internet protocol (IP) client a rapid, efficient restoration after a link failure; however its inability to protect against router failure erodes its attractiveness. Here, we propose a joint IP/optical restoration mechanism addressing this problem.

articleTitle: Novel birefringence compensating AWG design
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We propose a novel birefringence compensating arrayed waveguide grating (AWG) design that utilizes birefringence dependence on core width. We successfully demonstrated a polarization insensitive 100 GHz-spaced 16-channel multiplexer with a polarization dependent wavelength shift of 0.01 nm.

articleTitle: An adaptive decision threshold control of the optical receiver for multi-gigabit terrestrial DWDM transmission systems
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: An adaptive decision threshold control scheme for multigigabit terrestrial optical amplifier transmission system is applied to a 2.5 Gb/s optical receiver. Significant BER performance improvement was achieved over 600 km transmission experiment. We have studied and developed a practical technique for maximize the, signal to noise ratio (SNR) at the decision circuit by an adaptive threshold control (ATC). Transmission experiment has been carried out over 600 km fibers, and significant BER improvement has been attained.

articleTitle: 3 Tbit/s (300/spl times/11.6Gbit/s) transmission over 7380 km using C+L band with 25GHz channel spacing and NRZ format
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: Capacity increase is a constant request from long-haul submarine cable operators. This paper reports transmission capacity of 3 Tbit/s over 7380 km using 300 NRZ channels with 25 GHz channel spacing over the C+L band. The line used is composed of 10 fiber sections and 11 C+L EDFAs and operates in a recirculating loop configuration.

articleTitle: All-optical signal processing for 160 Gbit/s/channel OTDM/WDM systems
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: This paper describes the state-of-the-art technologies and issues of all-optical signal processing for implementing OTDM/WDM systems with a channel bit-rate of 160 Gbit/s.

articleTitle: Simultaneous 3R regeneration and wavelength conversion using a fiber-parametric limiting amplifier
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We present a 3R regenerator with simultaneous functionality of wavelength conversion. It consists of a fiber-parametric limiting amplifier and a phase-locked loop in a novel configuration. The 10 Gbit/s regenerator effectively reduces input signal noise and jitter.

articleTitle: Adjustable dispersion-slope compensator using entirely thin-film coupled-cavity allpass filters in a multi-reflection parallel configuration
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: A novel multi-reflection device composed of two coupled-cavity filters in a parallel configuration is reported. The device provides adjustable dispersion slope between -0.9 and -16.5 ps/sup 3/ over a bandwidth of 3 nm.

articleTitle: Ultra long-haul DWDM: network economics
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: The network economics of incorporating ultra long-haul DWDM systems into an evolving transport network architecture are investigated from the perspective of a large global Service Provider.

articleTitle: Timing jitter tolerant all-optical modulator and demultiplexing systems incorporating pulse-shaping fiber Bragg gratings
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We demonstrate the use of a superstructured fiber Bragg grating to pre-shape optical pulses to obtain more optimal operation of nonlinear, all-optical switches. Specifically, we demonstrate the conversion of 2.5 ps soliton pulses into 20 ps rectangular pulses at the input to both fiber and semiconductor optical amplifier (SOA-) based switches and show that rectangular switching windows can be achieved thereby providing a 5-10-fold reduction in timing jitter sensitivity.

articleTitle: 40 GHz all-optical XOR with UNI gate
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: 40 GHz Boolean XOR is demonstrated using an ultrafast nonlinear interferometer (UNI) gate. The gate operates with low switching energy and signals from the same source. It may be used in networking applications without wavelength conversion.

articleTitle: Application of asynchronous amplitude histograms for performance monitoring of RZ signals
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: It is shown that error evaluation from asynchronously sampled RZ amplitude histograms is possible for Gaussian noise irrespective of the duty cycle. Non-Gaussian perturbations such as timing jitter can be identified from the shape of the histograms.

articleTitle: Long-haul WDM NRZ transmission at 10.7 Gb/s in S-band using cascade of lumped Raman amplifiers
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We demonstrate the first S-band long-haul WDM transmission using a cascade of dispersion compensating lumped Raman amplifiers. Twenty NRZ channels, spanning the entire S-band, were transmitted over 10 spans of standard single-mode fiber (SSMF) (867 km) at 10.67 Gb/s, each achieving BER<10/sup -12/ without FEC.

articleTitle: Experimental demonstration of composite packet switching on a WDM photonic slot routing network
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We propose photonic slot routing ring networks that use a novel packet stacking technique to add/drop packets, which are simultaneously time and wavelength division multiplexed. Packet stacking, routing, and unstacking with four wavelengths was successfully demonstrated.

articleTitle: A comparative study of OBS and OFS
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: This paper evaluates the performance of two promising approaches for IP over WDM networks, namely optical burst switching (OBS) and optical flow switching (OFS), based on both synthetic and real traffic. We show that there is significantly better throughput when using OBS rather than OFS. We believe that this is a result of more efficient just-enough-time bandwidth reservation scheme used in OBS.

articleTitle: Optical packet switch with partially shared buffers: design principles
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We analyze the performance of an optical packet switch with partially shared buffers and we show that dimensioning of the switch predominantly depends on the number of packets that need to be buffered.

articleTitle: Performance comparison between DSB and VSB signals in 20 Gbit/s-based ultra-long-haul WDM systems
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: Transmission performance of double sideband (DSB) and vestigial sideband (VSB) signals was compared for the first time in 20 Gbit/s-based ultra-long-haul WDM transmission systems. Impact of channel spacing, repeater output power variation and terminal dispersion compensation error was investigated.

articleTitle: 1.05 Tbit/s WDM transmission over 8,186 km using distributed Raman amplifier repeaters
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We have achieved a 1.05 Tera bit/s WDM transmission over 8186 km using distributed Raman amplifier repeaters. Signal bandwidth was 31.2 nm and the optical SNR improvement was about 1.5 dB in contrast to using an EDFA repeater.

articleTitle: All-optical erasable storage buffer based on parametric nonlinearity in fiber
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We present an erasable all-optical buffer based on parametric gain and cross-phase modulation loading. The buffer is erased by employing a loop-mirror as a switch. We demonstrate storage of 1Gb/s packets for 1 ms.

articleTitle: Design optimization of dispersion compensating fiber for NZ-DSF considering nonlinearity and packaging performance
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: Design optimization of dispersion compensating fibers for NZ-DSFs considering both nonlinearity and bending performance required for packaging has revealed that a high FOM and low nonlinearity are achievable simultaneously by choosing proper design parameters.

articleTitle: A 160-km transparent metro WDM ring network featuring cascaded erbium-doped waveguide amplifiers
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We demonstrate a 4/spl times/2.5 Gb/s WDM ring with network-sourced virtual rings comprising optically shared wavelengths. The ring's four nodes feature erbium-doped waveguide amplifiers (EDWAs), shown here for the first time in cascade, which promise future integrability.

articleTitle: Tunable dispersion equalizer with a divided thin film heater
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We developed tunable dispersion equalizer with a chirped fiber grating and a divided thin film heater composed thirty-two thin film heaters. The divided thin film heater took an important role in the control of dispersion and dispersion slope, moreover the correction of group delay ripples. We successfully demonstrated the dispersion change from -304 ps/nm to -196 ps/nm and the dispersion slope change from +100 ps/nm/sup 2/ to -300 ps/nm/sup 2/.

articleTitle: Spectral broadening of double Rayleigh backscattering in a distributed Raman amplifier
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We observe broadening of the double Rayleigh backscattering (DRBS) spectrum in a Raman amplifier. This effect is caused by pump intensity fluctuations combined with proper fiber dispersion and can significantly reduce DRBS multipath interference crosstalk.

articleTitle: An optical implementation of a packet-based (Ethernet) MAC in a WDM passive optical network overlay
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We propose and demonstrate an optical implementation of an Ethernet (CSMA/CD) MAC on a WDM PON using spectrally slicing and novel AWG wiring connections. Fairness and throughput are demonstrated and compared to theory and simulations.

articleTitle: Ultra high-speed wavelength conversion and regeneration using semiconductor optical amplifiers
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: Techniques for all optical wavelength conversion and regeneration using semiconductor optical amplifiers are reviewed. In SOA based optical signal processing two (or more) signals are launched into the SOA where they interact due to the nonlinear properties of the active region in gain saturation, allowing the amplitude and phase of one optical signal to be controlled by another optical signal. Depending on the input conditions and topology, this can result in cross gain modulation, cross phase modulation or four wave mixing.

articleTitle: IP control of optical networks: design and experimentation
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: This paper describes an experimental demonstration of IP control of optical resources, highlighting key design and implementation choices for topology discovery, IP-based signaling, optical cross connect (OXC) control and rapid restoration.

articleTitle: Generation and interaction of parabolic pulses in high gain fiber amplifiers and oscillators
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: Parabolic pulses are generated from ultrashort pulse amplification in a high gain normal dispersion fiber amplifier. The pulses are robust against interactions and collisions and can be conveniently generated in a fiber laser configuration.

articleTitle: Athermal polarization-independent all-polymer arrayed waveguide grating (AWG) multi/demultiplexer
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: An athermal and polarization-independent arrayed-waveguide grating (AWG) multi/demultiplexer relying on an all-polymer approach was realized by properly adjusting the coefficient of thermal expansion of the substrate and the thermo-optic coefficient of the waveguide material.

articleTitle: IP over WDM network traffic engineering demonstration and experimentation
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: Traffic-engineering solutions that effectively exploit WDM reconfigurability are urgently needed for IP/WDM networks. This paper describes the testbed and software developed and demonstrated under the DARPA NGI SuperNet NC&M Project, and reports traffic-engineering experiments conducted over the testbed.

articleTitle: 40 Gbit/s eye pattern of a photoreceiver OEIC with monolithically integrated spot size converter
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: A combination of an InP-based monolithically integrated photoreceiver with a spot size converter is presented. A total receiver conversion gain of more than 1A/W, an extended bandwidth of 47 GHz for error corrected 40 Gbit/s application are achieved.

articleTitle: A 70 nm wide S-band amplifier by cascading TDFA and Raman fibre amplifier
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: A hybrid amplifier designed for short wavelength amplification is reported by cascading a Thulium doped fluoride fibre with a discrete Raman amplifier. Gain >20 dB for a bandwidth 1445-1520 nm was achieved.

articleTitle: Field trial over a 750 km long transparent WDM link using an adaptive 10 Gb/s receiver with non-intrusive monitoring capability
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: An adaptive optical receiver was successfully tested over a 750 km long transparent WDM link. The excellent agreement of estimated and measured bit error ratio demonstrates nonintrusive monitoring in a transparent optical network. We report on the results of a field trial over a 75 km long WDM link between Darmstadt and Berlin, with an adaptive 10 Gb/s optical receiver, that combines non-intrusive error rate monitoring, automatic receiver parameter optimization and adaptive mitigation of transmission impairments.

articleTitle: Germany-wide DWDM field trial: transparent connection of a long haul link and a multiclient metro network
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We report on error-free multiclient transmission over a Germany-wide all-optical, configurable DWDM system. The performance of the transparent connection of a metropolitan area network and a bi-directional long haul system is investigated under real-world conditions. We report on the topology of SIEMENS part of the Germany-wide field trial KOMNET and results of transparent interconnections between different optical domains.

articleTitle: From 40 to 80 10 Gbit/s DWDM transmission for ultra long-haul terrestrial transmission above 3000 km
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We report transmission results of 40 to 80 channels at 10 Gbit/s over a terrestrial SMF fiber map with above 80 km spans. From 3000 to 4000 km can be reached while leaving about a 4 dB system margin.

articleTitle: Theoretical investigation of fiber Raman amplifier with dynamic gain control
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: A gain-clamped fiber Raman amplifier is proposed and simulated. The results show that, gain variation of less than 0.2 dB over 70 nm bandwidth is obtainable for signal power variation of 18 dB.

articleTitle: Statistical dependence between first and second-order PMD
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We measure the first and the second-order polarisation mode dispersion (PMD) in high-PMD fiber, and determine correlation between the first and second-order PMD. Theory and measurements are in a good agreement. We follow a definition of two second-order components of second order PMD: component parallel to PMD vector, called polarization dependent chromatic dispersion (PCD), and perpendicular to the PMD vector component, causing depolarization. We investigate the statistics of both components of second order PMD vector as functions of differential group delay.

articleTitle: Radiation effects in optical communication devices
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We measure the ionizing radiation induced optical loss in different fiber-optic communication devices and evaluate the total optical loss in a multimode fiber link for application in high total dose nuclear environments.

articleTitle: Optimal pumping schemes for gain-band management of thulium-doped fiber amplifiers
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: It is shown that, used in conjunction with 1550-nm pumping, 1047-nm pumping is more suitable to operate the TDFA in the short wavelength band while 1400-nm pumping is more efficient for the long wavelength band.

articleTitle: Using grooming cross-connects to reduce ADM costs in SONET/WDM ring networks
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We show that the cost of electronic multiplexing in SONET/WDM rings can be reduced using small SONET cross-connects at multiple nodes. Our architecture uses multiple hub nodes and achieves significant savings over single hub architecture.

articleTitle: Optical signal processing for very high speed (>40 Gbit/s) ETDM binary NRZ clock recovery
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: Simulations and experiments show the application of optical signal processing instead of electrical nonlinear signal processing for the clock recovery in high bitrate (>40 Gbit/s) digital NRZ transmission systems. An electrical clock signal with high spectral purity can be obtained.

articleTitle: 160 Gbit/s transmission over 116 km field-installed fiber using 160 Gbit/s OTDM and 40 Gbit/s ETDM
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We report the first 160 Gbit/s RZ transmission experiment over field-installed standard fiber G.652 with optical 160 Gbit/s to 40 Gbit/s demultiplexing (OTDM) and subsequent electrical signal processing (ETDM) and we compare these results with 160 Gbit/s to 10 Gbit/s OTDM demultiplexing experiments.

articleTitle: Broadband dispersion and dispersion slope compensation in high bit rate and ultra long haul systems
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: This presentation reviews the essentials of dispersion compensating technology for nonzero dispersion shifted fibers. The implications of using the various existing technologies are discussed. Three recent developments in the world of long haul transmission has required one to re-evaluate the nature of dispersion compensation in NZ-DSF based systems. These are: increased bandwidth (> 32 nm), ultra long haul transmission distances (distances in excess of 2000 km) on land and 40 Gbps systems. All of the above, dramatically change the dispersion compensation requirement. We will discuss the different solutions that have been proposed in the literature to achieve the required dispersion compensating characteristics with primary emphasis being on dispersion compensating fiber.

articleTitle: Distributed amplification: how Raman gain impacts other fiber nonlinearities
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: The gain and noise figure of distributed amplifiers can be integrated and lumped at the end of each fiber span. This paper investigates whether this convenient simplification is valid in the presence of fiber nonlinearities. Distributed Raman amplification affects other fiber nonlinearities by changing the evolution of signal power along the fiber. Depending on system parameters can impact on self phase modulation and four wave mixing when gain is greater than -15 dB and increases the signal-to-signal Raman power transfer for all system at much lower gain values.

articleTitle: High-power cladding pumped erbium-ytterbium co-doped fiber laser
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: Cladding pumped erbium-ytterbium fiber lasers (EYDFL) in different free-running configurations have been described. We obtained slope efficiency of up to 50% with respect to absorbed pump power and an output power of 16.8 W.We study the influence of fiber length and pump wavelength in cladding-pumped erbium-ytterbium doped fiber lasers. We reached up to 16.8 W of output power from an EYDFL pumped through both ends at 915 nm. We believe this to be the highest-power EYDFL described in the literature. The slope efficiency was up to 50% with 915 nm pumping and 38% with 980 nm pumping,, both with respect to absorbed pump power.

articleTitle: Transport performance of a transparent WDM regional area ring network utilizing optimized components/fiber
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We present excellent performance results (Q-factor>10) for a transparent regional-size ring network based on application-optimized optical layer components and fiber. The network consists of 6 nodes interconnected with 86.5 km-spans of uncompensated negative dispersion fiber (520 km-ring circumference n no dispersion compensation) and supports 32 directly modulated channels operating at 2.5 Gb/s (80 Gb/s capacity).

articleTitle: Multi Gbit/s, high-sensitivity all silicon 3.3 V optical receiver using PIN lateral trench photodetector
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We report a 3.3 V silicon optical receiver consisting of a CMOS-compatible lateral trench PIN photodiode and a transimpedance amplifier that achieved a sensitivity of -17. 1 dBm at 2.5 Gb/s and demonstrated error-free (BER<10/sup -10/) operation up to 6.5 Gb/s at 845 nm. This is the highest reported sensitivity at data rates above 2.0 Gb/s and the fastest operation of any Si-based optical receiver.

articleTitle: Raman amplification in broadband WDM systems
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: After comparing Raman and erbium amplification, this talk focuses on why distributed Raman amplification has become a catalyzing technology to ultra-long 10 Gb/s and future 40 Gb/s transmission. A review of how Raman systems work and recent transmission results underscore's it's potential.

articleTitle: Optical sampling measurement with all-optical clock recovery using mode-locked diode lasers
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: Optical sampling measurement of 160-Gbps signals incorporating all-optical clock recovery has been demonstrated. External-cavity mode-locked semiconductor laser modules, which directly generate coherent 2-ps optical pulses, were used for optical clock recovery and as an optical sampling pulse source. We accomplished the real-time observation of waveform distortion in 160-Gbps optical data signals due to nonlinear optical effect in the transmission fiber.

articleTitle: 40 GHz actively mode-locked DBR laser diodes with a wide (800 MHz) locking range
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: 40-GHz active mode-locking of a monolithic DBR laser diode integrated with an electroabsorption modulator has been reported. Nearly transform-limited pulses of < 6 ps are generated over a frequency range of 37.7-38.5 GHz.

articleTitle: Impact of self-phase modulation on bandwidth efficient modulation formats
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We present the influence of self-phase modulation on duobinary and single sideband modulation. Additionally we determine and compare the receiver sensitivity for a bit error ratio of 10/sup -9/ varying fiber length and input power.

articleTitle: Optical metropolitan area networks
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: This paper discusses emerging issues in the development of future optical metropolitan area networks and describes the pioneering research at Stanford University to address some of them. The optical MAN space is seeing great innovation in industry and research. Trends such as network-wide reconfiguration, Internet protocol (IP) over WDM transport, tunable OADMs and novel fibers will emerge at the networking and physical layers. Through our four MAN networking projects, the Stanford OCRL has made a significant contribution to this innovation, which will help build powerful and exciting optical MANs.

articleTitle: Statistics of PMD-induced power fading for double sideband and single sideband subcarrier-multiplexed signals
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We experimentally and numerically compare the statistics of power fading for double sideband (DSB) and single sideband (SSB) subcarrier-multiplexed signals under high polarisation mode dispersion (PMD) conditions (average differential group delay (DGD) 40 ps) with and without dynamic first-order polarisation mode dispersion (PMD) compensation. We find that both SSB-SCM and DSB-SCM subcarrier multiplexed signals exhibit similar sensitivity to PMD-induced power fading. Reduces the worst case fading penalty by -20 dB.

articleTitle: Optimization of 40 Gbit/s dispersion maps for long-haul WDM transmissions with up to 0.4 bit/s/Hz spectral efficiency
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We numerically study optimal line dispersion management for 40 Gbit/s-based long-haul transmission systems, when considering first single-channel, and second WDM systems with 200 GHz and 100 GHz channel spacing.

articleTitle: Demonstration of 640 Gbit/s /spl times/ 7000 km submarine transmission system technology ready for field deployment
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: Transmission of 640 Gbit/s over 7000 km in a circulating loop experiment is achieved using all undersea qualified component and transmission fiber technology. We demonstrate an average system margin >5 dB, adequate to ensure the manufacturability of the system, employing 28 nm EDFA design, chirped return-to-zero (CRZ) modulation format, and a strong foward error correction (FEC) coding.

articleTitle: 10 Gb/s transmission using an electroabsorption-modulated distributed Bragg reflector laser with integrated semiconductor optical amplifier
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We demonstrate for the first time a 10 Gb/s EA-modulated wavelength-selectable DBR laser module with an integrated semiconductor optical amplifier. Transmission over 82 km of standard fiber with -3 dBm average power on 20 channels spaced by 50 GHz is achieved.

articleTitle: Optical noise figure: theory and measurements
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We examine the concept of optical noise figure in to two-port devices. Definitions of noise figure are discussed along with applications of noise figure to circuits incorporating cascades of amplifiers and other optical and optoelectronic devices.

articleTitle: A flow-routing approach for optical IP networks
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: A novel flow-routing approach with the feature of retaining packet sequence is proposed for optical Internet protocol (IP) networks. Analytical results demonstrate its effectiveness in increasing the good-throughput of the router especially during the congestion period.

articleTitle: A highly nonlinear holey fiber and its application in a regenerative optical switch
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We report the fabrication of a highly nonlinear, polarization-maintaining, silica holey fiber with an effective area of /spl sim/2.5 /spl mu/m/sup 2/ at 1550 nm. Nonlinear switching is demonstrated in a 3.3 m long regenerative switch based on SPM with appropriate band pass filtering.

articleTitle: To spread or not to spread-the myths of optical CDMA
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We compare the wisdom of CDMA technique in cellular radio and optical networks, and discuss the fundamental challenges in optical CDMA systems.

articleTitle: Efficient dual-wavelength Raman fiber laser
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: A Raman fiber laser emitting simultaneously at 1426 and 1456 nm (1.2 W total power) is described and used to demonstrate a Raman gain of 18.5 dB with </spl plusmn/0.9 dB ripple over the C-band.

articleTitle: Over-40-GHz modulation bandwidth of EAM-integrated DFB laser modules
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: Electroabsorption modulator (EAM)-DFB modules with record high bandwidth of 41 GHz have been developed. 40 Gb/s NRZ operation with 12 dB extinction ratio and 40 GHz short pulse trains with 6 ps pulse width have been successfully achieved.

articleTitle: Flip chip bonded optoelectronic devices on ultra-thin silicon-on-sapphire
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We describe flip chip bonding of arrayed optoelectronic devices (VCSELs, MSM and PIN detectors) onto ultra-thin silicon-on-sapphire (UTSi). We present results of UTSi optical transmitters and receivers for 2.5 Gbps (and higher) parallel optical links.

articleTitle: High sensitive optical sampling oscilloscope simultaneous coverage of both C and L bands
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: An optical sampling oscilloscope with SFG conversion efficiency as high as 15 times that of KTP, while simultaneously covering both the C and L bands, is demonstrated for the first time.

articleTitle: 2.56 Tbit/s (40 Gbit/s/spl times/64 WDM) unrepeatered 230 km transmission with 0.8 bit/s/Hz spectral efficiency using low-noise fiber Raman amplifier and 170 /spl mu/m/sup 2/-Aeff fiber
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We have demonstrated 50 GHz-spaced 40 Gbit/s/spl times/64 WDM unrepeatered transmission over 230 km using a low-noise Raman amplifier, 170 /spl mu/m/sup 2/-Aeff fiber and bandlimited RZ signals without polarization-demultiplexing at the receiver. 2.56 Tbit/s capacity was transmitted with only 25.8 nm bandwidth.

articleTitle: 40 Gbit/s return-to-zero transmission over 500 km of standard fiber using chirped fiber Bragg gratings with small group delay ripples
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: A 40 Gbit/s return-to-zero (RZ) transmission has been successfully achieved over 500 km using standard fibers (non dispersion shifted fiber, SMF) and chirped fiber Bragg gratings (CFBG). We fabricated CFBGs with small group delay ripples, and achieved error free transmission (BER<1/spl times/10/sup -12/) using these CFBGs for dispersion compensation.

articleTitle: Ultrafast synchronous all-optical time division multiplexing system demonstration
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We present a synchronous optical time division multiplexing system capable of fully loaded packet transmission. Novel slot architecture provides network-wide self-synchronization and novel system architecture provides enhanced network reliability. We demonstrate receiver functionality with multilayered interdependent all-optical logic.

articleTitle: Classification of two-link failures for all-optical networks
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: Studies the relationship between failure localization and the properties of link restoration algorithms for mesh networks through an examination of recovery from multiple failures.

articleTitle: Centralized vs. distributed on-demand bandwidth reservation mechanisms in WDM ring
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: A bandwidth efficient way to cope with the highly bursty traffic of the Internet is to resort to on-demand fast reservation of optical circuits (or lightpaths). Taking into consideration the data burst size, signaling dynamics and network latency, the paper compares performance of centralized versus distributed reservation mechanisms for WDM ring.

articleTitle: 4-port interleavers and fully circulating bi-directional circulators
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: A low-loss 4-port interleaver was demonstrated. The device becomes a 4-port fully-circulating wavelength-interleaving bi-directional circulator with the addition of a non-reciprocal element. This new device technology opens up a range of possibilities for bi-directional fiber devices.

articleTitle: Transmission of 1550 nm 10 Gb/s directly modulated signal over 100 km of negative dispersion fiber without any dispersion compensation
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We demonstrate the largest transmission distance (100 km) ever reported for a 10 Gb/s 1.55 /spl mu/m directly modulated signal over a single fiber link without using any dispersion compensation. The fiber is optimised for operation with directly modulated lasers and has negative dispersion.

articleTitle: Coolerless operation of 980 nm pump modules
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: Efficient fiber Bragg grating wavelength and power stabilization of 980 nm pump lasers at high fiber-coupled output power (150 mW at 75/spl deg/C and 95 mW at 100/spl deg/C) over a wide temperature range of 90/spl deg/C is demonstrated.

articleTitle: 3.2 Tb/s field trial (80/spl times/40 Gb/s) over 3/spl times/82 km SSMF using FEC, Raman and tunable dispersion compensation
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: A record aggregate capacity transmission of 3.2 Tb/s (80/spl times/40 Gb/s) audio, video and data traffic in a single fiber over 3 spans of SSMF (standard single mode fiber) was demonstrated in a field trial using forward error correction (FEC), Raman amplification and tunable dispersion compensation (TDC).

articleTitle: Novel cascaded optical coding schemes for bandwidth efficient systems applications
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: A new technique for advanced optical coding based on multi-level subcarrier modulated signals is demonstrated in a cascaded modulator. Enhanced transmission in a spectrally efficient 300 m multimode fibre link is achieved.

articleTitle: Fundamental limitation and optimization on optical code conversion for WDM packet switching networks
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: Fundamental performance limitation originated from multi-access interference on a generic code converter for WDM packet switching networks is derived and analyzed. A closed-form optimal threshold value that yields the lowest code conversion error is also given.

articleTitle: Laser-diode-pumped highly-efficient gain-shifted thulium-doped fiber amplifier operating in the 1480-1510-nm band
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We have developed a gain-shifted thulium-doped fiber amplifier with high-optical-efficiency (29%) and high-output-power (+21.5 dBm) operating in the 1480-1510-nm wavelength band by employing a novel laser-diode pumping scheme of 1.4 and 1.56 microns.

articleTitle: Very fast chromatic dispersion measurement using lightwave synthesized frequency sweeper and lock-in detection with phase diversity technique
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: The authors propose a chromatic dispersion measurement method that uses a lightwave synthesized frequency sweeper. This method features a very fast measurement time and good wavelength accuracy when measuring group delay.

articleTitle: Enhanced PMD mitigation using forward-error-correction coding and a first-order compensator
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We demonstrate that forward-error-correction combined with a first-order compensator can greatly improve system performance over a wide range of polarisation mode dispersion (PMD). Both the experimental and theoretical results show that the system PMD tolerance limit can be increased to more than 40 ps in 10 Gb/s systems.

articleTitle: High-birefringent photonic crystal fiber
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: A highly birefringent photonic crystal fiber design is analysed. Birefringence up to 10/sup -3/ is found. Random fluctuations in the cladding design are analysed, and the fiber is found to be a feasible polarization maintaining fiber.

articleTitle: Penalty-free error-free all-optical data pulse regeneration at 84 Gbps with symmetric-Mach-Zehnder-type regenerator
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We have achieved penalty-free data pulse regeneration at 84 Gbps down to an error rate level of 10/sup -11/ with a pseudorandom data pattern length of 2/sup 31/-1 for a time division multiplexing (TDM) optical communication system. An all-optical interferometric semiconductor regenerator was used.

articleTitle: Upgradeable metro networks using frequency-cyclic optical add/drop
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We present a strategy for graceful capacity upgrades in optical ring networks, based on passive wavelength add/drop modules which are frequency-cyclic. The concept is demonstrated by incorporating a frequency-cyclic node in a five-node metro-scale ring, and characterizing the bit-error rates of multiple 2.5 Gb/s data streams.

articleTitle: High-speed optical protection system using MEMS optical switch triggered by SONET performance monitor
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: High-speed and low cost optical 1+1 protection system using a MEMS optical switch triggered by SONET performance monitor (SD/SF) for high accuracy protection was developed. 980 /spl mu/s switching time of optical power recovery was demonstrated.

articleTitle: Uncooled, 10 Gb/s operation of two-contact InGaAsP lasers with low drive current
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: Uncooled, high-speed modulation of two-contact lasers is presented with ultra-low drive currents. Practical operation at 10 Gb/s up to temperatures of 85/spl deg/C and extinction ratios of 6 dB are found for current swings which are less than 40% of conventional lasers.

articleTitle: New dispersion-flattened hybrid optical fiber link composed of medium-dispersion large-effective-area fiber and negative dispersion fiber
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: A new dispersion-flattened hybrid optical fiber link composed of a medium-dispersion large-effective-area fiber and a negative dispersion fiber is presented. The hybrid fiber link showed a very low and flat dispersion in the C-band. We present a new enlarged-effective-area positive dispersion fiber (EE-PDF) with a medium-dispersion to reduce the dispersion accumulation and a NDF with a negative dispersion slope optimized for dispersion compensation for the EE-PDF. In addition we report on the dispersion and attenuation characteristics of a hybrid optical fiber link composed of these fibers.

articleTitle: Large bandwidth, highly efficient mode coupling using long-period gratings in dispersion tailored fibers
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: We report the demonstration of strong (>20 dB) coupling in long-period fiber-gratings over bandwidths as large as 43 nm. These novel spectra are obtained by suitably tailoring the dispersion properties of a fiber. The polarization dependent coupling for the mode-converters varies by less than 0.004% over the entire spectrum.

articleTitle: High power optical amplifiers for CATV applications
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: Optical power for analog/digital CATV is obtained from cladding pumped Yb,Er-doped fibre amplifiers where broad area laser diodes are free-space coupled through a hybrid isolator to an all-silica double clad gain fiber.

articleTitle: Novel all-optical 10 Gbp/s RZ-to-NRZ conversion using SOA-loop-mirror
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: The authors propose and demonstrate a novel all-optical return-to-zero (RZ) to non-return-to-zero (NRZ) data format conversion using a semiconductor optical amplifier (SOA) loop mirror. Error free transmission up to 78 km for the NRZ format converted data at 10 Gb/s is achieved. Also, the proposed method shows better transmission performance than the conventional Mach-Zehnder modulation method.

articleTitle: High brightness cavity-controlled surface emitting GaInAs lasers operating at 980 nm
publicationTitle: OFC 2001. Optical Fiber Communication Conference and Exhibit. Technical Digest Postconference Edition (IEEE Cat. 01CH37171)
abstract: Current high performance optical communication systems demand high power erbium doped fiber amplifiers. These amplifiers are powered by edge emitting 980 nm pump lasers, which are limited in optical power by catastrophic optical damage and require external gratings for wavelength stabilization. Conventional surface emitting lasers (Miller et al, 2000) have demonstrated very high powers from large apertures (320 /spl mu/m), but only in a highly multimode beam (/spl sim/3500 modes). In this paper, we report electrically pumped GaInAs surface emitting semiconductor lasers that have both the optical mode and the wavelength controlled by an extended cavity. These lasers have produced record power and brightness levels in both multi-mode and single-mode operation. Output power levels of more than 1 W CW from a multi-mode (beam quality parameter M/sup 2//spl sim/10-20) device and more than 500 mW CW in a TEM/sub 00/ mode (M/sup 2//spl sim/1.2) have been achieved.
